descriptionHtml:
Bitte beachte: Wir haben verschiedene Möglichkeiten in ganz Deutschland und benötigen Flexibilität bezüglich der Standorte. Wenn du dich für die Stelle bewirbst, gib bitte alle deine bevorzugten Standorte in Deutschland an.
Alle unsere Praktika finden vollständig vor Ort statt.

Amazon Operations ist das Rückgrat der Amazon-Kundenerfahrung. Mit über 50 Logistikzentren, hunderten von Zustellstationen und zehntausenden von Versandmitarbeiter:innen arbeitet das Team zusammen, um Artikel effizient an Kund:innen zu liefern. In den Logistikzentren werden jährlich Millionen von Artikeln kommissioniert und verpackt, während die Zustellteams daran arbeiten, Bestellungen pünktlich an die Kund:innen zu bringen. Sicherheit hat oberste Priorität, und die Betriebskultur ist geprägt von Teamwork, Vielfalt und einer gemeinsamen Arbeitsethik, die das Geschäft reibungslos am Laufen hält. Das Team ist stolz darauf, den Qualitätsservice zu liefern, für den Amazon weltweit bekannt ist.


Hinweis: Du musst zum Starttermin die Arbeitsberechtigung für das Beschäftigungsland haben.

Key job responsibilities
Als Amazon Operations-Praktikant:in hast du die Möglichkeit, deine analytischen Fähigkeiten in wirkungsvollen Projekten anzuwenden, die die Funktionalität und den Service von Logistikzentren, Sortierzentren und Zustellstationen verbessern. Wichtige Aspekte der Rolle umfassen:

• Abschluss von Projekten mit hoher Priorität nach höchstem Standard und Nachweis deiner Fähigkeit, Ergebnisse zu liefern
• Datenanalyse zur Identifizierung operativer Herausforderungen und Verbesserungsmöglichkeiten
• Vorschlagen und Testen von Lösungen in Zusammenarbeit mit dem Team zur Umsetzung der effektivsten Ansätze
• Entwicklung von Kommunikations- und Teamfähigkeiten durch die Zusammenarbeit mit Führungskräften, Stakeholdern und Versandmitarbeiter:innen.
• Bewegung im Gebäude, um mit verschiedenen Teams zu interagieren. Das umfasst aktives Wissenssammeln durch Teilnahme an Aktivitäten wie Vorbesprechungen, Ablaufmeetings und Diskussionen mit dem Führungsteam und Versandmitarbeiter:innen.
• Die Fähigkeit, sich im Arbeitsbereich zu orientieren und zwischen verschiedenen Bereichen zu wechseln, ist für diese Position unerlässlich.
• Flexibilität bei verschiedenen Arbeitszeiten und Schichtmustern nach Bedarf zeigen.
• Möglicher Umzug an den vorgesehenen Arbeitsort.

A day in the life
Unsere Praktika sind Bildungsmöglichkeiten, die es dir als unserer zukünftigen Führungskraft ermöglichen, zu entdecken, wie wir unsere Teams von Versandmitarbeiter:innen führen und entwickeln. Du tauchst in die schnelllebige, komplexe Welt unserer Logistikzentren, Sortierzentren und Zustellstationen ein und erlebst, wie unsere Führungskräfte ihre Teams einsetzen, um Kundenerwartungen zu erfüllen.

Dieses Praktikum versetzt dich ins Herz unserer Abläufe und ermöglicht es dir, den Weg einer Kundenbestellung zu verfolgen. Du erhältst einen realistischen Einblick in die Vollzeitchancen, die dich in unserem Unternehmen erwarten.

Du lernst, wie unsere Führungskräfte eine sichere, produktive Umgebung schaffen und das volle Potenzial ihrer Teams durch effektive Einbindung und Leistungsmanagement-Strategien nutzen. Das ist deine Chance, Fähigkeiten zu entwickeln, die dich zu einer lohnenden Karriere bei Amazon führen werden.

About the team
Praktikant:innen-Community:

• Als Amazon-Praktikant:in bist du Teil einer lebendigen, unterstützenden Community, die dein Wachstum und deine Entwicklung fördert. Du arbeitest mit Praktikant:innen aus der ganzen Welt zusammen, knüpfst Kontakte und nimmst an sozialen Veranstaltungen teil, um deinen Horizont zu erweitern. Du kannst auch spezialisierten Gruppen beitreten, die sich auf Bereiche wie Nachhaltigkeit konzentrieren, um deine vielfältigen Interessen zu erkunden.
Unterstützung:
• Das Praktikumsprogramm bietet ein robustes Unterstützungssystem, einschließlich wöchentlicher Praktikant:innen-Sprechstunden, spezieller IT- und HR-Unterstützung sowie einem Programmteam, das sich deinem Erfolg verschrieben hat. Das stellt sicher, dass du die Anleitung und Hilfe hast, die du zum Gedeihen brauchst.
Lernsessions:
• Exklusive Lernsessions werden deine Fähigkeiten weiter verbessern und dir Zugang zu Amazons modernsten Lernplattformen und der Expertise von Branchenführern gewähren. Diese strukturierten Entwicklungsmöglichkeiten bereiten dich auf den nächsten Schritt in deiner Karriere vor.
Möglichkeiten:
• Nach erfolgreichem Abschluss des Praktikums kannst du für eine Absolvent:innen-Stelle oder ein zweites Praktikum in Betracht gezogen werden, was es dir ermöglicht, deine Reise mit Amazon fortzusetzen. Zusätzlich erhältst du ein wettbewerbsfähiges Monatsgehalt, Umzugsunterstützung und Zugang zu einer Reihe von Mitarbeitervorteilen.
Praktikums-Starttermine über das Jahr:
• Wir stellen Praktikant:innen ein, die jederzeit von Januar bis Juli 2026 anfangen können. Jeden Monat führen wir 1-2 Onboarding-Tage für neue Mitarbeiter:innen durch.

- Derzeit im vorletzten oder letzten Jahr und auf dem Weg zu einem Universitätsabschluss in Supply Chain, Business/Management, Ingenieurwesen oder einem anderen verwandten Bereich.

title: Processing Technician - 2nd Shift, Amazon Leo
descriptionHtml:
Amazon Leo is Amazon’s low Earth orbit satellite broadband network. Its mission is to deliver fast, reliable internet to customers and communities around the world, and we’ve designed the system with the capacity, flexibility, and performance to serve a wide range of customers, from individual households to schools, hospitals, businesses, government agencies, and other organizations operating in locations without reliable connectivity.

Export Control Requirement: Due to applicable export control laws and regulations, candidates must be a U.S. citizen or national, U.S. permanent resident (i.e., current Green Card holder), or lawfully admitted into the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum.

The success of Amazon Leo depends on the quality, reliability, cost, integration, throughput, and security of the products that you deliver. If you seek a fast-paced, dynamic environment; if you thrive on solving difficult problems where resolutions have high impact; and if you love the challenge of building something from scratch, then this role will be an ideal next career step. To be successful you need to be highly motivated and detail oriented while showing the highest standards of execution.



Key job responsibilities
• Primarily second-shift, but shift schedule may vary depending on production/processing/launch schedules
• Successfully process Amazon Leo satellites through receiving and electrical checkouts.
• Independently execute and prioritize work to meet production schedules
• Rigging and critical lifts of bulky, sensitive flight hardware
• Able to obtain and maintain licenses, operator permits, and/or certifications as required
• Use precision calibrated tools – torque wrenches, multimeters, optical inspection devices, micrometers, and calipers
• Read and interpret engineering drawings and technical documentation
• Perform work according to procedures, specifications, and test instructions
• Check and inspect your work after completion to ensure engineering and quality standards are met per the drawing and work instruction requirements
• Collaborate with manufacturing engineers to develop and document activities, including continuous improvement opportunities
• Perform other related duties, as assigned, for the purpose of ensuring an efficient, safe, and effective work environment
• Must be willing and able to perform extended travel, either domestically or internationally as business needs demand.

A day in the life
The Process Technician will work closely with cross-functional engineering, test, quality and operations teams on flight hardware integration processes. This position requires skill and experience in a variety of areas, including mechanical assembly, propellent loading, rigging, electrical checkouts and satellite troubleshooting. In short, you will be responsible for a majority of the most critical tasks to process and integrate the Kuiper satellite for launch, ensuring high quality, workmanship and safety standards are adhered to on a daily basis.

Valuable skills and experience for this role include a variety of aerospace operational disciplines, including mechanical assembly, propellant loading (or similar spacecraft pneumatic/propulsion operations), pneumatic and electrical control system troubleshooting/rework, and rigging/crane/forklift operations

Our team has a broad mix of experience levels and Amazon tenures, and we’re building an environment that celebrates knowledge sharing and mentorship.

- High school diploma or equivalent
- Can lift up to 49 pounds, stand/walk during shifts lasting up to 12 hours, and be able to frequently push, pull, squat, bend, and reach
- Experience with precision torque, measurement and inspection devices (i.e., automated and manual torque wrenches, calipers, micrometers, profilometers, optical inspection devices, multi-meters, torque wrenches)
- Experience in the aerospace/launch industry, automotive industry, medical device industry, aviation, military, or other high-reliability operating environment
- A demonstrated ability in reading/understanding technical drawings, work instructions, and standard operating procedures
- Able to stand for long periods of time and perform repetitive assembly operations
- Able to obtain and maintain a US Passport
- Able and willing to comply with the Government of French Guiana which mandates that travelers receive vaccinations
- Able to pass Kennedy Space Center background checks

Preferred qualifications

title: Engineering Operations Technician
descriptionHtml:
Join our dynamic team and become a critical guardian of technological infrastructure! As a Data Center Engineering Technician, you'll play a pivotal role in maintaining the heartbeat of mission-critical technology infrastructure, ensuring seamless operations that power global digital experiences. Your expertise will directly contribute to maintaining an extraordinary 99.999% uptime, keeping the digital world running smoothly and efficiently.

Engineering Technicians are Amazon’s front line when it comes to hands-on electrical and mechanical equipment troubleshooting. They will maintain, operate, and troubleshoot, Data Center Operation’s Mission Critical Facilities, which includes stand-by diesel generators and related fuel systems, as well as three phase electrical systems such as: switch gear, UPSs, PDUs, wet cell batteries and associated systems, CRAC, centrifugal chillers, cooling towers/water chemical system, air handlers and associated systems, pumps, & motors.

AWS Infrastructure Services owns the design, planning, delivery, and operation of all AWS global infrastructure. In other words, we’re the people who keep the cloud running. We support all AWS data centers and all of the servers, storage, networking, power, and cooling equipment that ensure our customers have continual access to the innovation they rely on. We work on the most challenging problems, with thousands of variables impacting the supply chain — and we’re looking for talented people who want to help.

You’ll join a diverse team of software, hardware, and network engineers, supply chain specialists, security experts, operations managers, and other vital roles. You’ll collaborate with people across AWS to help us deliver the highest standards for safety and security while providing seemingly infinite capacity at the lowest possible cost for our customers. And you’ll experience an inclusive culture that welcomes bold ideas and empowers you to own them to completion.

NOTE: PDX is an AWS GovCloud region. As required by our contracts with the federal government, effective February 24, 2026, logical access to the AWS GovCloud region will be restricted to Amazon employees who are U.S. Citizens. (GovCloud may NOT be accessed from outside of the United States).

NOTE: Lump sum stipend will be provided to eligible candidates who relocate for this position.

Key job responsibilities
- Daily building rounds to monitor and record information from electrical, mechanical, and fire/life safety equipment to ensure 24/7 reliability and availability
- Monitor Building Management Systems (BMS) and Electrical Power Management System (EPMS)
- Assist in troubleshooting of facility and rack-level events within internal Service Level Agreements (SLA)
- Perform rack installs and rack decommissioning within internal SLA
- Perform PM, troubleshooting, root cause analysis, and repair of electrical and mechanical equipment
- Technical writing to support change management program
- Monitor daily work requests and manage to resolution, and execute projects from conception to completion
- On-site support of contractors, sub-contractors and vendors, ensuring that all work performed is in accordance with established practices, procedures & local legislation
- Work schedule changes depending on specific site needs. Shifts can be up to 12-hours and may rotate on a predefined schedule. Some locations have on-call rotations.

Willingness and demonstrated ability to work in the following physical conditions with reasonable accommodations:

- Regularly walk, use hands and fingers, handle or feel, reach with hands and arms, stoop, kneel, crouch or crawl, climb stairs, twist, bend, work above shoulders, grasp, carry, push and pull objects into position

title: Software Development Manager, Transact
descriptionHtml:
Join our Transact organization as a Software Development Manager and shape how Amazon moves critical data across regions, enabling services to operate with greater flexibility and resilience. You'll lead a talented engineering team in designing and deploying innovative data movement solutions that reduce latency for customers worldwide and strengthen our infrastructure against regional failures.

Key job responsibilities
- Lead and develop your engineering team to design, develop, deploy, and support key features of data movement tools while maintaining current system stability
- Drive architectural initiatives that enable services to operate across regions while retaining critical business functions within specific regions
- Build and nurture your team through recruiting, hiring, mentoring, and fostering a positive team culture where engineers grow and thrive
- Connect with customers and cross-functional partners regularly to gather requirements, build the team roadmap, and collaborate with product and partner teams on new projects

A day in the life
As a Software Development Manager in the Transact organization, you'll balance strategic leadership with hands-on technical engagement. Your day might include collaborating with your engineering team on architectural decisions for data movement tools, connecting with customers to understand their evolving needs, and working alongside product and partner teams to refine the roadmap. You'll mentor engineers through complex technical challenges, participate in design reviews that shape our multi-region strategy, and help navigate the trade-offs between supporting current systems and building next-generation capabilities. Your work directly impacts how Amazon's services—from Stores to Prime Video—operate reliably across the globe.

About the team
We are a team of builders focused on providing Amazon with foundational technologies for transaction storage, configuration management, and safe data movement. Our work supports critical Amazon businesses and helps teams adopt evolving AWS and non-AWS technologies. We partner closely with AWS teams to improve public offerings while maintaining a commitment to robust, scalable solutions delivered with engineering best practices. We value simplicity, reliability, and solutions that "just work" for millions of people using Amazon's products daily. When you join us, you'll be part of a collaborative group that appreciates the importance of infrastructure that enables other teams to delight customers.

Basic qualifications

- 7+ years of engineering experience
- 3+ years of engineering team management experience
- 8+ years of leading the definition and development of multi tier web services experience
- Knowledge of engineering practices and patterns for the full software/hardware/networks development life cycle, including coding standards, code reviews, source control management, build processes, testing, certification, and livesite operations
- Experience partnering with product or program management teams

- Experience in communicating with users, other technical teams, and senior leadership to collect requirements, describe software product features, technical designs, and product strategy

title: Area Manager Intern - Summer 2027 (AL, FL, GA, NC, SC), University Recruiting
descriptionHtml:
Power that runs the world | Discover careers in Operations

Operations roles at Amazon put you at the center of how things move from a click to a doorstep. You'll help design, improve, and run systems that connect people, products, and places, at scale. You'll take ownership early, work closely with teams to solve real-world challenges, and see the direct results of your decisions as they reach customers every day. Here, the impact of what you build isn't abstract, it's visible, immediate, and meaningful - keeping one of the world's most complex operations moving forward. This is where your journey takes shape through action, responsibility, and the opportunity to grow in many directions.

This is not a corporate, remote or office-based position. This is a ten-week internship (40 hours per week) during the summer of 2027 located within one of Amazon’s fulfillment centers, sort centers, delivery stations or other operations buildings. Amazon is seeking customer focused individuals eager to develop a collaborative leadership style with a team of hourly employees across our Operations network! Our warehouses are fast-paced supply chain environments where standing, walking, and having on-the-production floor conversations are common.

As an Area Manager Intern, you will have the opportunity to learn how to coach, motivate and mentor a team of Amazon associates in a warehouse environment. Amazon provides extensive training and development to become an exceptional people leader. Your main focus will be learning to manage a team as well as developing a summer project in partnership with your site leadership.

Term: 10 weeks

Benefits: Access to Amazon's Medical Advice Line, Employee Assistance Program (EAP), and financial benefits.

Visit www.aboutamazon.com/workplace/facilities to find more information on each of our building types.

Please note we are not able to provide sponsorship now or in the future for these positions. Eligible candidates must have work authorization without employer intervention to be considered.

This posting encompasses all openings in the state(s) listed in title. Site placement is matched by aligning your location preferences with location availability after your interview. Summer relocation and housing assistance provided if eligible.

Key job responsibilities
• Learn to coach, manage and develop a team of 50-100 Amazon Associates.
• Drive standard work and continuous improvement through an intern project.
• Work independently and operate in an autonomous environment.
• Stand/walk during shifts lasting up to 12 hours.
• Willing and able to regularly work shift patterns that include nights, weekends, and/or holidays based on business needs. While shifts vary site to site, most follow a fixed 4-day work week with 3 days off.
• Oversee truck deliveries, handle and sort packages using pallet jacks, operate PIT equipment (at applicable facilities) and step in as needed.
• Work in an environment where the noise level varies.
• Lift up to 49 pounds and frequently push, pull, squat, bend and reach.
• Climb and descend stairs (when applicable).

A day in the life
As an Area Manager intern, no two days look exactly the same, but every shift gives you the chance to learn how to lead a team, solve real problems, and directly impact how millions of customers receive their orders.

Start of Shift: Set the Tone
• Shadow a current Area Manager and begin to:
• Get a handoff from the outgoing manager and review what's carrying over so nothing falls through the cracks.
• Lead a team huddle to kick off the shift. Huddles are used to align on goals, safety priorities, and key focus areas.
• Confirm your team is in place, positioned for success, and ready to go before operations begin.

Middle of Shift: Lead from the Floor
• Walk the floor regularly to stay connected to your team, spot issues early, and keep things running smoothly.
• Drive results across safety, quality, and productivity — balancing all three in real time.
• Adjust staffing and resources as volume and priorities shift throughout the day.
• Coach and develop your team members, respond to challenges as they come up, and partner with support teams to remove roadblocks.
• Keep peers and leadership informed on how the shift is tracking and flag risks before they become problems.
• Develop your internship project.

End of Shift: Close Strong
• Do a final walkthrough to make sure your area is clean, organized, and set up for the next team's success.
• Review your shift's performance data and capture what went well and what to improve
• Hand off to the incoming manager with a clear picture of priorities, open items, and next steps.
• Wrap up any remaining administrative tasks so you leave the shift with a clean slate.

Every shift, you'll see the direct results of your leadership: from the energy of your team to the packages that reach customers' doorsteps. This is where your decisions have real, visible impact.

Basic qualifications

- Currently enrolled in a bachelor’s degree program with all requirements anticipated to be completed between December 2027 and August 2028.

Preferred qualifications

- Strong communication skills, both verbal and written.
- Excellent customer service and interpersonal skills.
- Currently enrolled in a Bachelor's program for Supply Chain, Business/Management, Engineering or another related field.

descriptionHtml:
Do you aim to have a dynamic impact on the world?

Are you up for creating solutions and solving tomorrow’s problems today?

Then we have the opportunity for you!

We’re seeking an efficient ICQA Operations Manager to take ownership of our fulfillment center Inventory Control and Quality Assurance (ICQA). Our fulfillment centers sit at the heart of Amazon’s rapidly growing operations network: they are where we manage our fast-moving inventory. In each fulfillment center, our teams stow deliveries, pick products, package them up and ship them out; each of these groups have played their part in taking us where we are today.

title: Area Manager Intern – Summer 2027 (MO, OH, KY)
descriptionHtml:
Power that runs the world | Discover careers in Operations

Operations roles at Amazon put you at the center of how things move from a click to a doorstep. You'll help design, improve, and run systems that connect people, products, and places, at scale. You'll take ownership early, work closely with teams to solve real-world challenges, and see the direct results of your decisions as they reach customers every day. Here, the impact of what you build isn't abstract, it's visible, immediate, and meaningful - keeping one of the world's most complex operations moving forward. This is where your journey takes shape through action, responsibility, and the opportunity to grow in many directions.

This is not a corporate, remote or office-based position. This is a ten-week internship (40 hours per week) during the summer of 2027 located within one of Amazon’s fulfillment centers, sort centers, delivery stations or other operations buildings. Amazon is seeking customer focused individuals eager to develop a collaborative leadership style with a team of hourly employees across our Operations network! Our warehouses are fast-paced supply chain environments where standing, walking, and having on-the-production floor conversations are common.

As an Area Manager Intern, you will have the opportunity to learn how to coach, motivate and mentor a team of Amazon associates in a warehouse environment. Amazon provides extensive training and development to become an exceptional people leader. Your main focus will be learning to manage a team as well as developing a summer project in partnership with your site leadership.

Term: 10 weeks

Benefits: Access to Amazon's Medical Advice Line, Employee Assistance Program (EAP), and financial benefits.

Visit www.aboutamazon.com/workplace/facilities to find more information on each of our building types.

Please note we are not able to provide sponsorship now or in the future for these positions. Eligible candidates must have work authorization without employer intervention to be considered.

This posting encompasses all openings in the state(s) listed in title. Site placement is matched by aligning your location preferences with location availability after your interview. Summer relocation and housing assistance provided if eligible.

Key job responsibilities
• Learn to coach, manage and develop a team of 50-100 Amazon Associates.
• Drive standard work and continuous improvement through an intern project.
• Work independently and operate in an autonomous environment.
• Stand/walk during shifts lasting up to 12 hours.
• Willing and able to regularly work shift patterns that include nights, weekends, and/or holidays based on business needs. While shifts vary site to site, most follow a fixed 4-day work week with 3 days off.
• Oversee truck deliveries, handle and sort packages using pallet jacks, operate PIT equipment (at applicable facilities) and step in as needed.
• Work in an environment where the noise level varies.
• Lift up to 49 pounds and frequently push, pull, squat, bend and reach.
• Climb and descend stairs (when applicable).

A day in the life
As an Area Manager intern, no two days look exactly the same, but every shift gives you the chance to learn how to lead a team, solve real problems, and directly impact how millions of customers receive their orders.
Start of Shift: Set the Tone
• Shadow a current Area Manager and begin to:
• Get a handoff from the outgoing manager and review what's carrying over so nothing falls through the cracks.
• Lead a team huddle to kick off the shift. Huddles are used to align on goals, safety priorities, and key focus areas.
• Confirm your team is in place, positioned for success, and ready to go before operations begin.
Middle of Shift: Lead from the Floor
• Walk the floor regularly to stay connected to your team, spot issues early, and keep things running smoothly.
• Drive results across safety, quality, and productivity — balancing all three in real time.
• Adjust staffing and resources as volume and priorities shift throughout the day.
• Coach and develop your team members, respond to challenges as they come up, and partner with support teams to remove roadblocks.
• Keep peers and leadership informed on how the shift is tracking and flag risks before they become problems.
• Develop your internship project.
End of Shift: Close Strong
• Do a final walkthrough to make sure your area is clean, organized, and set up for the next team's success.
• Review your shift's performance data and capture what went well and what to improve
• Hand off to the incoming manager with a clear picture of priorities, open items, and next steps.
• Wrap up any remaining administrative tasks so you leave the shift with a clean slate.
Every shift, you'll see the direct results of your leadership: from the energy of your team to the packages that reach customers' doorsteps. This is where your decisions have real, visible impact.

Basic qualifications

- Currently enrolled in a bachelor’s degree program with all requirements anticipated to be completed between December 2027 and August 2028.

Preferred qualifications

- Strong communication skills, both verbal and written.
- Excellent customer service and interpersonal skills.
- Currently enrolled in a Bachelor's program for Supply Chain, Business/Management, Engineering or another related field.

title: Senior Finance Analyst, WW Ops FP&A - strategic planning
descriptionHtml:
Are you ready to shape the financial future of one of the world's most complex supply chains? Amazon is seeking a Financial Analyst II to drive critical decision-making through deep analytics and financial modeling at the intersection of operations and business strategy. In this role, you'll build AI-native workflows that transform how we analyze costs, forecast trends, and influence senior stakeholders across a highly matrixed organization.

This position offers a unique opportunity to develop long-term financial models for Amazon's cost structure while working on logistics innovation. You'll have the chance to build, improve, and standardize processes and systems that impact business performance at scale, all while expanding your expertise in the world's most sophisticated supply chain operations.

descriptionHtml:
In pursuit of being Earth's Best Employer, our global Human Resources teams, known as People eXperience and Technology (PXT), drive business success by fostering a safe, inclusive, and innovative culture. The HR Partner role offers an exceptional opportunity to build your career in human resources, focusing on employee experience, engagement, leadership development and HR operational excellence.

As an HR Partner on the NASC PXT team, you will support PXT operations through consistent standard work execution, relationship-building, and timely issue resolution. With a visible presence across site operations, you'll foster team culture, support engagement, and coach leaders on PXT practices. You'll create positive employee experiences while building your skills in navigating increasingly complex issues and influencing without authority. Success in this role comes from building strong partnerships, demonstrating sound judgment, and maintaining a customer-centric approach. You'll learn to use data-driven insights and HR technologies to enhance the employee experience while developing core HR capabilities that will serve as the foundation for your career growth.

You will be expected to work onsite at an Amazon facility.

Key job responsibilities

title: Principal Pgm Mgr - Amazon Shipping, Amazon Shipping
descriptionHtml:
Who are we?
Ready to build Amazon's next $100B business? We're not just entering shipping—we're transforming how billions of packages move around the globe. By evolving Amazon's legendary fulfillment engine into an agile, intelligent shipping network, we're creating a resilient system that continuously optimizes to deliver on time, every time, for every business and every customer. Every shipment is more than just a box—it spins the flywheel faster, continuously enhancing our logistics network through scale, speed, and intelligence. As we increase density and reach, we're revolutionizing shipping for ALL businesses while simultaneously strengthening Amazon's own delivery capabilities—reducing costs and accelerating deliveries across our entire ecosystem.

The NODE (network operations and delivery experience) team owns the final mile—the last, most visible, and most operationally complex leg of the delivery journey. This is where the promise we make to customers is kept: the package on the doorstep, on time, at the lowest possible cost. We build and optimize the systems, routing intelligence, and delivery operations that move packages from the last delivery station to the customer's hands across a rapidly scaling global network.

What will you do?
We're hiring a Principal Program Manager for our NODE team to drive cross-organizational initiatives, influence VP-level roadmaps, and unlock hundreds of millions in cost savings and delivery performance through transformational improvements to our final mile network and delivery experience.

You'll operate with complete autonomy to identify and remediate endemic problems in our last-mile operations, drive architectural and operational decisions across Product, Commercial, Engineering, and Operations organizations, and establish the strategic mechanisms that enable Amazon Shipping to scale final mile delivery at the pace our business demands.

Working at the unique intersection where program leadership directly impacts delivery cost, speed, and reliability, you'll define multi-year operational and technical roadmaps, influence resource allocation across VP organizations, and solve significantly complex problems where both business and operational strategies are undefined.

You'll collaborate closely with:

Product Management teams defining final mile capabilities and roadmaps
Commercial teams driving enterprise shipper adoption and delivery SLAs
Engineering organizations building routing, dispatch, and delivery platforms
Operations teams running delivery stations and last-mile networks globally
Principal Engineers and Architects on routing, capacity, and network design decisions
VP-level leadership across multiple organizations
Who are you?
You're a seasoned program management leader with deep operational fluency in last-mile logistics and delivery networks, combined with exceptional strategic judgment and a proven ability to build consensus across diverse executive stakeholders. You have a track record of managing programs that span multiple VP organizations, operating independently in highly ambiguous environments where both the problem and the solution are undefined.

Key attributes:

Strategic thinker who connects operational and technical improvements to delivery cost and customer experience outcomes
Depth in final mile operations, route optimization, capacity planning, and distributed logistics systems
Executive presence with the ability to influence VP-level audiences
Data-driven decision maker who defines meaningful success metrics (cost per package, on-time delivery, delivery defects)
Strong owner who takes accountability for business impact beyond project delivery
Exceptional communicator who translates complex operational and technical concepts clearly
Proven ability to identify and remediate endemic problems at scale
You thrive in fast-paced, ambiguous environments where operational decisions directly impact delivery cost and the customer experience for millions of packages a day. You're passionate about solving endemic problems that affect global last-mile operations while creating the playbook that scales Amazon Shipping's final mile worldwide.

Key job responsibilities
Strategic Program Leadership & Roadmap Ownership

Own the end-to-end strategy and execution for Amazon Shipping's final mile network, working across Product, Commercial, Engineering, and Operations VP organizations to drive operational and architectural decisions and organizational alignment
Define multi-year operational and technical roadmaps for final mile improvements that directly impact delivery speed, cost per package, on-time delivery rates, and delivery defect reduction
Influence resource allocation and technology investments across multiple organizations to ensure alignment with final mile strategy
Identify and remediate endemic problems that create delivery bottlenecks, limit network scalability, or cause recurring delivery defects, decomposing significantly complex challenges into straightforward solutions
Cross-Organizational Influence & Executive Engagement

Build consensus across VP organizations through effective narratives and presentations, representing complex operational and technical trade-offs clearly
Manage executive-level escalations with excellent judgment, balancing operational constraints with business priorities
Drive alignment between final mile goals and organizational objectives across global stakeholders
Partner with Principal Engineers and SDMs to ensure routing, dispatch, and capacity decisions scale to match business growth projections
Operational & Technical Excellence

Drive large-scale programs that solve complex problems in route optimization, capacity planning, dispatch, delivery tracking, exception handling, and driver/delivery-partner tooling
Evaluate network and system designs for scalability, delivery performance, safety, and operational excellence
Lead simplification initiatives that enable delivery-station and operations teams to operate independently and reduce operational and technical debt
Manage large-scale engineering and operations efforts that remediate endemic final mile problems with network-wide impact
Metrics, Visibility & Business Impact

Establish and own success metrics that connect operational and technical improvements to business outcomes (cost per package, on-time delivery, delivery defect rate, delivery speed, customer delivery experience)
Create mechanisms for continuous visibility and proactive risk identification across the final mile network
Own quarterly business reviews that translate operational metrics into business impact for executive audiences
Quantify the business impact of final mile improvements and communicate ROI to leadership
Team Development & Community Building

Amplify impact by creating and optimizing critical mechanisms that enable teams to deliver independently
Actively develop the program management community through mentoring, promotion assessments, and knowledge sharing
Raise the bar for program management excellence across Amazon Shipping
Streamline processes and drive adoption of best practices across multiple organizations

A day in the life
Your mornings start with strategic analysis—spotting patterns across the final mile network and quantifying business impact. You review delivery performance metrics, cost-per-package trends, on-time delivery rates, and delivery defect data to identify emerging trends and opportunities.

Mid-morning involves writing VP-level documents that drive operational and technology roadmaps and priorities. You craft narratives that connect delivery improvements to business outcomes, preparing for upcoming reviews and decision-making forums.

Afternoons focus on driving initiatives: partnering with Principal Solution Architects and SDMs on routing, capacity, and network design decisions, influencing cross-org priorities, and preparing narratives for executives. You facilitate alignment meetings, resolve blockers, and ensure programs stay on track.

Late afternoons are spent managing escalations and engaging with operations and enterprise partners. You work directly with delivery-station leaders and key shippers experiencing final mile challenges, translating their feedback into actionable improvements.

Throughout the day, you shift between diving deep on operational and technical problems and influencing stakeholders on business impacts. You balance strategic thinking with tactical execution, ensuring both immediate delivery wins and long-term network evolution.

You'll collaborate with engineering leaders building our adaptive delivery technology, operations teams executing our delivery promise on the ground, commercial stakeholders focused on scaling our shipper base, and product managers defining the future of final mile. This role demands someone who can toggle between strategic vision and tactical execution, turning last-mile challenges into opportunities for transformation.

Basic qualifications

- 7+ years of working cross functionally with tech and non-tech teams experience
- 7+ years of program or project management experience
- 7+ years of managing, analyzing and communicating results to senior leadership experience
- Bachelor's degree
- Experience implementing repeatable processes and driving automation or standardization
- Experience defining program requirements and using data and metrics to determine improvements

Preferred qualifications

- Experience delivering projects within scope, time, budget and quality

title: Corporate Counsel, Real Estate, Real Estate Legal
descriptionHtml:
Amazon is seeking a strategic, business-minded real estate attorney to support the development, expansion, and management of our Grocery and Physical Stores portfolio—including Whole Foods Market, One Medical, and other physical retail formats—as well as manufacturing facilities and Worldwide Operations sites. You'll work on some of the most dynamic and varied real estate deals across Amazon's physical footprint, directly impacting our ability to serve customers in stores and through our supply chain.





Key job responsibilities
- Lead legal strategy on complex commercial real estate transactions including retail leases, ground leases, build-to-suit agreements, purchase and sale agreements, and development contracts for grocery stores, physical retail locations, manufacturing facilities, and operations sites
- Serve as strategic legal advisor to business partners across Grocery, Physical Stores, Manufacturing, and Worldwide Operations on real estate acquisitions, lease negotiations, and development projects
- Identify and proactively flag legal and business risks in real estate transactions, providing practical solutions that balance risk mitigation with operational needs
- Manage and direct outside counsel on specialized matters including title review, survey analysis, environmental due diligence, and complex lease negotiations—maintaining oversight of legal strategy, quality, and costs
- Advise on land use, zoning, entitlements, and permitting strategies to support store development, manufacturing expansions, and operations facilities across multiple regulatory environments
- Collaborate with cross-functional teams including Store Development, Design, Operations, Finance, Tax, Construction, and Environmental to drive projects from site selection through store opening or facility launch
- Structure creative deal solutions for novel legal and business challenges across Amazon's growing grocery, retail, manufacturing, and operations real estate portfolio
- Support post-acquisition and post-lease-execution matters including construction contracts, property management agreements, landlord disputes, and ongoing operational real estate issues
- Drive process improvements and leverage technology to increase efficiency and scalability across Amazon's growing physical stores and operations real estate portfolio
- Stay current on real estate laws, regulations, and industry trends affecting retail, grocery, manufacturing, and industrial development

A day in the life
Your day might start on a call with outside counsel negotiating a new Whole Foods Market lease and aligning with clients on key terms. By mid-morning, you've pivoted to reviewing a purchase and sale agreement for an operations facility, flagging title issues and coordinating with the business team on diligence timelines. After lunch, you're collaborating with Store Development and Finance teams to structure a creative lease solution for a multi-format grocery concept. That afternoon, you're on a cross-functional call with the Economic Development team reviewing a developer's disclosed tax incentive to confirm Amazon's compliance obligations are properly scoped. Before end of day, you're back in lease-mode, directing outside counsel on co-tenancy language in a new store deal while simultaneously advising business partners on a landlord dispute at an existing location. Throughout the day, you balance urgent matters with strategic work, making high-judgment calls that directly impact Amazon's ability to grow our physical presence and serve customers.



About the team
You'll join Amazon's Real Estate Legal team, a dynamic group supporting one of the world's most diverse and fast-growing real estate portfolios. Our team supports grocery stores, physical retail formats, manufacturing facilities, and operations sites. We value strategic thinking, business partnership, and creative problem-solving. You'll work closely with experienced real estate attorneys and have exposure to senior leadership on high-profile projects.

Basic qualifications

- Juris Doctor and membership in one state bar or equivalent
- 5+ years of post bar admission legal experience
- Experience in Real Estate Law

Preferred qualifications

- Experience in real estate transactions
- Experience of a mix of corporate law firm and in-house work
- Experience in development, land use or economic development
- Proven ability to identify legal issues proactively and provide strategic guidance to business stakeholders
- Experience managing or directing outside counsel on real estate matters
- Comfortable making high-judgment decisions in ambiguous situations
- Experience with retail, grocery, manufacturing, or large-scale industrial real estate projects
- Expertise in land use, zoning, entitlements, or economic development matters
- Ability to drive process improvements and increase efficiency and scaling in legal operations
- Excellent written and verbal communication skills with ability to translate complex legal concepts for business audiences

title: Data Center Technician , DCC Communities
descriptionHtml:
AWS Infrastructure Services owns the design, planning, delivery, and operation of all AWS global infrastructure. In other words, we’re the people who keep the cloud running. We support all AWS data centers and all of the servers, storage, networking, power, and cooling equipment that ensure our customers have continual access to the innovation they rely on. We work on the most challenging problems, with thousands of variables impacting the supply chain — and we’re looking for talented people who want to help.

You’ll join a diverse team of software, hardware, and network engineers, supply chain specialists, security experts, operations managers, and other vital roles. You’ll collaborate with people across AWS to help us deliver the highest standards for safety and security while providing seemingly infinite capacity at the lowest possible cost for our customers. And you’ll experience an inclusive culture that welcomes bold ideas and empowers you to own them to completion.

We are looking for Data Center Technicians to join our expanding Infrastructure Operations team. Data Center Technicians are the primary resolver and troubleshoot and solve a range of datacenter infrastructure issues including, but not limited to: hardware, fiber, networking, and related problems. You will be part of the Data Center Operations (DCO) team, overseeing the operation and maintenance of the IT infrastructure and hardware for data centers in AWS Cloud regions. You will become the primary resolver for your support team, and gain troubleshooting skills on different hardware and software cases. You will be able to troubleshoot and solve most infrastructure issues and engage other appropriate solutions groups on more complex problems to drive solutions..



Key job responsibilities
• SAFETY

Follow and maintain the highest safety standards and diligently encourage a world-class safety culture. Own the safety initiatives and projects to foster a strong safety culture.

• DATA CENTER OPERATIONS (DCO)

This position involves:
- Diagnosing hardware and network problems followed by physical repairs
- Troubleshooting events within internal Service Level Agreements (SLAs)
- Performing root cause analysis of equipment failures
- Manual handling and lifting of equipment may be required (weight limits in accordance with regulations)
- Working rotating shifts (morning/night) as well as weekends to maintain the 24/7 data center environment

A valid (EU) driving license is required as Data Centers may not have any public transportation available nearby.

Location Requirements:
Our data centers are located in remote areas where access via public transport may be limited. Therefore, a valid EU driving license is required for this role.

Work Schedule:
This is a 100% onsite in-person position due to the hands-on nature of managing mission-critical infrastructure and data center industry.

A day in the life
In this role, you'll be working on our advanced ticketing system, managing a diverse workload and solving complex server hardware issues.

You'll be part of a collaborative team that keeps our cloud infrastructure running smoothly, responding to both automated directives and team leadership with exceptional time management and adaptability.

Your expertise in problem ticket tracking and escalation procedures will be crucial as you consistently meet and exceed Amazon's high standards for technical proficiency and operational excellence. This role is vital in maintaining the efficiency and reliability of our sophisticated data center infrastructure – you'll be working and supporting the face of Cloud technology in the region.

We're looking for skilled technicians with a passion for technology to help us expand our Cloud to the next level.

About the team
Diverse Experiences
AWS values diverse experiences. Even if you do not meet all of the preferred qualifications and skills listed in the job description, we encourage candidates to apply. If your career is just starting, hasn’t followed a traditional path, or includes alternative experiences, don’t let it stop you from applying.

Why AWS?
Amazon Web Services (AWS) is the world’s most comprehensive and broadly adopted cloud platform. We pioneered cloud computing and never stopped innovating — that’s why customers from the most successful startups to Global 500 companies trust our robust suite of products and services to power their businesses.

Inclusive Team Culture
AWS values curiosity and connection. Our employee-led and company-sponsored affinity groups promote inclusion and empower our people to take pride in what makes us unique. Our inclusion events foster stronger, more collaborative teams. Our continual innovation is fueled by the bold ideas, fresh perspectives, and passionate voices our teams bring to everything we do.

Mentorship & Career Growth
We’re continuously raising our performance bar as we strive to become Earth’s Best Employer. That’s why you’ll find endless knowledge-sharing, mentorship and other career-advancing resources here to help you develop into a better-rounded professional.

Work/Life Balance
We value work-life harmony. Achieving success at work should never come at the expense of sacrifices at home, which is why we strive for flexibility as part of our working culture. When we feel supported in the workplace and at home, there’s nothing we can’t achieve in the cloud.

- General knowledge of troubleshooting.

title: Duales Studium - BWL
descriptionHtml:
Ein Job im Operations-Bereich bei Amazon versetzt dich ins Zentrum dessen, wie Dinge vom Klick bis zur Haustür gelangen. Du hilfst dabei, Systeme zu entwerfen, zu verbessern und zu betreiben, die Menschen, Produkte und Orte miteinander verbinden – und das in großem Maßstab. Du übernimmst früh Verantwortung, arbeitest eng mit Teams zusammen, um reale Herausforderungen zu lösen, und siehst die direkten Ergebnisse deiner Entscheidungen, wenn sie täglich bei den Kunden ankommen. Hier ist die Wirkung dessen, was du aufbaust, nicht abstrakt – sie ist sichtbar, unmittelbar und bedeutsam – und hält eine der komplexesten Betriebsorganisationen der Welt am Laufen. Hier nimmt deine Reise Gestalt an – durch Handeln, Verantwortung und die Möglichkeit, in viele Richtungen zu wachsen Dein Einstieg in die Führung - Das Duale Studium bei Amazon
- Studiengang: BWL / Logistikmanagement (B.A.)
- Studienpartner: IU Internationale Hochschule (30+ Standorte deutschlandweit)
- Programmbeginn: 1. August 2027
- Dauer: 3,5 Jahre
- Einsatzorte: mehr als 20 Amazon-Standorte in Deutschland (Fulfillment Center und Sort Center)
Das duale Studium bei Amazon ist ein strukturiertes Führungsentwicklungsprogramm, das dich Schritt für Schritt auf eine operative Führungsrolle vorbereitet. Wer das Programm erfolgreich abschließt, hat die Chance direkt eine Position als Area Manager:in in unserem Netzwerk zu bekommen - ohne weiteres Bewerbungsverfahren.
________________________________________
Drei Phasen auf dem Weg zur Führungskraft
Das Programm ist in drei aufeinander aufbauende Phasen gegliedert, die deinen Verantwortungsbereich kontinuierlich erweitern.
Phase 1 - Operative Grundlagen: Zunächst lernst du die operativen Abläufe im Fulfillment Center von Grund auf kennen, analysierst Kennzahlen und setzt eigenständig Projekte zur Prozessverbesserung um.
Phase 2 - Rotation & Führungsentwicklung: Anschließend rotierst du durch verschiedene operative Bereiche, übernimmst schrittweise Führungsaufgaben - von der Begleitung der Team Leads über Schichtplanung bis hin zur Personalsteuerung - und entwickelst ein Verständnis für bereichsübergreifende Zusammenhänge.
Phase 3 - Area-Manager-Niveau: In der Abschlussphase arbeitest du auf Area-Manager-Niveau: Du steuerst operative Kennzahlen, führst Teams eigenständig und trägst echte Verantwortung für deinen Bereich.

Das bieten wir dir
• Karriereperspektive: Nach erfolgreichem Abschluss des Programms wechselst du direkt in eine Area Manager Position im Amazon-Netzwerk - ohne erneutes Bewerbungsverfahren
• Studienfinanzierung: Amazon übernimmt die Studiengebühren an der IU
• Mentoring: Strukturierte Begleitung durch Learning Manager:in und operative Führungskräfte
• Netzwerk: Zugang zu einem europaweiten Operations-Netzwerk
• Mobilität: Kostenloses Deutschlandticket
• Verpflegung: Bezuschusste Mahlzeiten am Standort
• Mitarbeitervorteile: Vielfältige Vorteile, wie ein Amazon Mitarbeiterrabatt
• Technologie: Arbeite täglich mit modernster Automatisierungs- und Robotiktechnologie

Key job responsibilities
• Analyse und Optimierung operativer Prozesse in Fulfillment- und Sortierbereichen
• Eigenständige Durchführung von Continuous Improvement Projekten mit messbaren Ergebnissen
• Übernahme von Führungsaufgaben im Rahmen von Lead-Rotationen (Schichtverantwortung, Teamsteuerung, KPI-Management)
• Mitarbeit an bereichsübergreifenden Projekten in den Bereichen Arbeitssicherheit, Prozessoptimierung, Personalwesen und Technik
• Vorbereitung auf die eigenständige Steuerung eines operativen Bereichs als Area Manager:in
• Enge Zusammenarbeit mit einem internationalen Team innerhalb des europäischen Amazon-Netzwerks

A day in the life
Deine Betreuung im Programm
Du bist nicht allein. Während des gesamten Programms wirst du von zwei Seiten unterstützt:
• Dein:e Learning Manager:in am Standort begleitet dich durch alle drei Phasen, ist deine zentrale Ansprechperson und koordiniert deine Entwicklung
• Operative Führungskräfte mentoren dich während deiner Rotationen und geben dir direktes Feedback aus der Praxis
Zusätzlich bist du Teil einer deutschlandweiten Community dualer Student:innen - ein Netzwerk, das mit dir wächst.

________________________________________
Dein Alltag: Theorie und Praxis im Wochentakt
Das Studium läuft parallel zur Praxis - keine langen Blockphasen, sondern ein wöchentlicher Rhythmus:
• 2 Tage Studium an deinem IU-Standort (Logistik, Supply Chain, BWL, Personalführung)
• 2-3 Tage / 20 Stunden im Amazon Fulfillment Center oder Sort Center

Du bist kein Besucher im Betrieb. Du bist Teil des Teams - von Tag eins an.

- Allgemeine Hochschulreife, Fachhochschulreife / fachgebundene Hochschulreife
- Fließende Deutschkenntnisse in Wort und Schrift (C1-Niveau)
- Fortgeschrittene Englischkenntnisse in Wort und Schrift (B2-Niveau)
- Affinität für das Fach Mathematik
- Umgang mit MS-Office (insbesondere Kenntnisse in Excel, Word und PowerPoint)

Preferred qualifications

- Ausgeprägte Kommunikationsfähigkeit
- Eigeninitiative, Vorbildfunktion und „Hands-on-Mentalität"
- Interesse, Führungsverantwortung zu tragen

title: Finance Manager, WW Operations Working Capital & Free Cash Flow
descriptionHtml:
Amazon's WW Operations Finance FP&A team is seeking a Finance Manager to own the Working Capital and Free Cash Flow agenda for our Insights, Planning, Analytics and Technology team. This is a highly visible, senior individual contributor role supporting senior finance and operations leaders, with end-to-end ownership of the worldwide operations working capital and free cash flow position.

At Amazon, we are working to be the world's most customer-centric company, and our Operations network is renowned for being world-class, delivering packages to customers across the globe. Behind that network sits one of the largest working capital and cash flow positions at the company, and how we plan, forecast, and optimize it directly shapes the free cash flow Amazon reports to investors.

You will own the worldwide free cash flow and working capital planning and reporting cycle from start to finish, translate complex cash movements into narratives that senior leaders act on, and drive the mechanisms that make cash forecasting more accurate and more automated over time. You will not simply report the numbers. You will decide what they mean, hold the line in front of senior leadership, and influence how regional and central teams plan cash across organizations you do not directly control.

The successful candidate will have exceptional communication and analytical skills, the ability to dive deep and succinctly communicate findings to senior leaders, and comfort operating with a high degree of autonomy in a dynamic, fast-paced environment. You should hold a high bar on professional integrity, be energized by ambiguity, and be passionate about using data to solve big, complex cash flow problems.

Key job responsibilities
- Own end-to-end planning, forecasting, reporting, and controllership of worldwide operations working capital and free cash flow, holding accuracy and timeliness to a senior-leader-review standard.
- Author the free cash flow and working capital review documents presented to senior leadership, drive those reviews directly, and translate complex cash movements into clear narratives and recommendations.
- Own cash capital expenditure forecasting for worldwide operations, partnering with regional finance, supply chain, and treasury teams to phase spend accurately and close methodology gaps that affect the reported cash position.
- Drive automation and process improvement across the forecasting and reporting framework, including science-based forecasting approaches, and partner with shared services to scale mature workstreams.
- Identify incomplete or inaccurate data, determine root causes, implement escalation plans, and make sound judgment calls in ambiguous environments where data is difficult to procure.
- Influence senior leaders and cross-functional partners outside the direct reporting line, and mentor and develop analysts as the team scales.

A day in the life
You start the day reviewing worldwide cash flow and working capital performance, flagging where the forecast is moving and why. You spend part of the morning aligning a regional partner on an inventory or payables assumption, then translate it into a crisp recommendation for an upcoming senior leadership review. In the afternoon you pressure-test a cash capital expenditure phasing question with a regional team, work with a partner to harden a forecasting mechanism so the reporting cycle runs cleanly, and coach an analyst through a variance analysis. Throughout, you are deciding what matters, holding controllership, and shaping the cash narrative leaders rely on.

About the team
As part of the WW Operations FP&A team, you will join a collaborative and knowledgeable group that is passionate about numbers, data, and how to use them to generate insight and improve the business. We are the trusted business advisors who earn trust through accurate, reliable financial insight, and we work in a supportive environment where expertise is shared freely and Invent and Simplify is highly encouraged. The working capital and free cash flow workstream sits at the center of governance and executive cash narrative for worldwide operations, giving this role direct exposure to the most senior finance and operations leaders.

title: Sr. Product Manager, AWS Kubernetes
descriptionHtml:
Containers are redefining how customers build, deploy, and run applications. The Amazon Container Services team is looking for a Senior Product Manager (Technical) to help define the future of Kubernetes on AWS and accelerate container adoption in the cloud.

You will own product strategy and development across a set of EKS product areas, with a focus on Bottlerocket, our Linux-based operating system built for running containers. That means everything from vision and feature definition through prioritization, positioning, and GTM/adoption.

We want someone who has solved real customer problems in Kubernetes, container runtimes, or developer platforms. You should have a track record of working backwards from customer needs and turning them into products that customers love.

Working closely with engineering teams, you will see the direct impact of your work on customers who run production workloads on Kubernetes at scale. This is a high-visibility role that interacts with all levels of AWS leadership.

Our ideal candidate brings familiarity with Kubernetes, container runtimes, or the node and OS layer that clusters run on. You understand the operational realities of running containers in production: provisioning, patching, upgrades, and security posture. You thrive in a fast-paced environment that requires strong technical and business judgment.

You will define product requirements and go-to-market strategy for the customers you serve. The role requires coordination across engineering, sales, partners, and solutions architecture. You'll work with customers, open-source communities, and software vendors to prioritize roadmap features and define new capabilities.

Key job responsibilities
- Own product strategy, roadmap, and feature definition for a set of EKS product areas, with Bottlerocket as a primary focus

- Work backwards from customer needs to define product requirements for cluster capabilities, node and runtime experience, and operational tooling

- Drive the Bottlerocket product roadmap: node lifecycle, upgrade experience, custom image building, ML/accelerator instance support, and observability integration

- Lead customer engagements to collect requirements and validate product direction

- Partner with engineering to prioritize and deliver features across the full product lifecycle, from concept through launch and adoption

- Build and execute go-to-market plans in coordination with sales, solutions architecture, partner teams, and developer advocacy

- Define and track success metrics for adoption, retention, and customer outcomes

- Write narratives (PR/FAQs, strategy docs, business reviews) to drive alignment and secure investment from leadership

- Represent EKS and Bottlerocket externally at customer meetings, industry events, and community forums

- Coordinate across AWS container services (ECS, ECR, Fargate) and adjacent compute teams

A day in the life
You start your week talking to customers who run production workloads on Kubernetes. You dig into what is working and what is not, then turn that into product requirements. You whiteboard with engineering and design to iterate on solutions. You define the roadmap, present strategy to leadership, and track metrics to spot opportunities. A good chunk of your time goes to the operating system that clusters run on: how nodes get built, patched, and upgraded. Some days you review documents or mentor peers. Other days you are on stage at a conference.

About the team
Our team builds the managed Kubernetes service used by hundreds of thousands of customers, from startups to the world's largest enterprises. descriptionHtml:

Key job responsibilities

About the Role

Account Management- Brand Specialist (Italian)

As a Brand Specialist as part of Amazon Vendor Services (AVS) Team of Retail Business Services, you will have the exciting opportunity to help shape and deliver on a strategy for managing Amazon AVS vendors.

AVS team is looking for a bright, customer obsessed, driven, and creative candidate to join our team. You will interface internally with leaders from our Retail and Vendor Services teams and will be responsible for all aspects of the vendor’s business with Amazon. You will engage directly with multiple internal teams to optimize the product line for key manufacturers (vendors) on Amazon.com. You will utilize a wide range of skills and work across major functional areas such as site merchandising, buying, inventory management, finance, operations and online marketing, to drive the performance of strategic vendor partners at Amazon. In this role you will be focused on the strategic and operational aspects of managing the customer relationships with our vendors.

You will conceive, create and analyze a wide range of marketing and site merchandising efforts, to include marketing campaigns to grow the vendor’s traffic, brand awareness, customer conversion, and revenue on Amazon. Also you will look into strategic and operational aspects of their business with Amazon, root cause analysis of issues and opportunities affecting the vendor’s business.

· Work with internal Amazon teams/vendors to improve operational aspects of their business in providing a great consumer experience

- Can manage multiple projects and meet deadlines

- - Excellent written and oral communication and presentation skills. Ability to express thoughts logically and succinctly.
- - Ability to work in teams and ultimately focus on delivering results with high standards

Preferred qualifications

- Bachelor's degree or equivalent
- - Exposure to retail buying, retail planning & allocation, product/project management, marketing or e-commerce will be a plus
- - SQL and VBA knowledge
- - Lean Six Sigma

title: Duales Studium - BWL
descriptionHtml:
Ein Job im Operations-Bereich bei Amazon versetzt dich ins Zentrum dessen, wie Dinge vom Klick bis zur Haustür gelangen. Du hilfst dabei, Systeme zu entwerfen, zu verbessern und zu betreiben, die Menschen, Produkte und Orte miteinander verbinden – und das in großem Maßstab. Du übernimmst früh Verantwortung, arbeitest eng mit Teams zusammen, um reale Herausforderungen zu lösen, und siehst die direkten Ergebnisse deiner Entscheidungen, wenn sie täglich bei den Kunden ankommen. Hier ist die Wirkung dessen, was du aufbaust, nicht abstrakt – sie ist sichtbar, unmittelbar und bedeutsam – und hält eine der komplexesten Betriebsorganisationen der Welt am Laufen. Hier nimmt deine Reise Gestalt an – durch Handeln, Verantwortung und die Möglichkeit, in viele Richtungen zu wachsen Dein Einstieg in die Führung - Das Duale Studium bei Amazon
- Studiengang: BWL / Logistikmanagement (B.A.)
- Studienpartner: IU Internationale Hochschule (30+ Standorte deutschlandweit)
- Programmbeginn: 1. August 2027
- Dauer: 3,5 Jahre
- Einsatzorte: mehr als 20 Amazon-Standorte in Deutschland (Fulfillment Center und Sort Center)
Das duale Studium bei Amazon ist ein strukturiertes Führungsentwicklungsprogramm, das dich Schritt für Schritt auf eine operative Führungsrolle vorbereitet. Wer das Programm erfolgreich abschließt, hat die Chance direkt eine Position als Area Manager:in in unserem Netzwerk zu bekommen - ohne weiteres Bewerbungsverfahren.
________________________________________
Drei Phasen auf dem Weg zur Führungskraft
Das Programm ist in drei aufeinander aufbauende Phasen gegliedert, die deinen Verantwortungsbereich kontinuierlich erweitern.
Phase 1 - Operative Grundlagen: Zunächst lernst du die operativen Abläufe im Fulfillment Center von Grund auf kennen, analysierst Kennzahlen und setzt eigenständig Projekte zur Prozessverbesserung um.
Phase 2 - Rotation & Führungsentwicklung: Anschließend rotierst du durch verschiedene operative Bereiche, übernimmst schrittweise Führungsaufgaben - von der Begleitung der Team Leads über Schichtplanung bis hin zur Personalsteuerung - und entwickelst ein Verständnis für bereichsübergreifende Zusammenhänge.
Phase 3 - Area-Manager-Niveau: In der Abschlussphase arbeitest du auf Area-Manager-Niveau: Du steuerst operative Kennzahlen, führst Teams eigenständig und trägst echte Verantwortung für deinen Bereich.

Das bieten wir dir
• Karriereperspektive: Nach erfolgreichem Abschluss des Programms wechselst du direkt in eine Area Manager Position im Amazon-Netzwerk - ohne erneutes Bewerbungsverfahren
• Studienfinanzierung: Amazon übernimmt die Studiengebühren an der IU
• Mentoring: Strukturierte Begleitung durch Learning Manager:in und operative Führungskräfte
• Netzwerk: Zugang zu einem europaweiten Operations-Netzwerk
• Mobilität: Kostenloses Deutschlandticket
• Verpflegung: Bezuschusste Mahlzeiten am Standort
• Mitarbeitervorteile: Vielfältige Vorteile, wie ein Amazon Mitarbeiterrabatt
• Technologie: Arbeite täglich mit modernster Automatisierungs- und Robotiktechnologie

Key job responsibilities
• Analyse und Optimierung operativer Prozesse in Fulfillment- und Sortierbereichen
• Eigenständige Durchführung von Continuous Improvement Projekten mit messbaren Ergebnissen
• Übernahme von Führungsaufgaben im Rahmen von Lead-Rotationen (Schichtverantwortung, Teamsteuerung, KPI-Management)
• Mitarbeit an bereichsübergreifenden Projekten in den Bereichen Arbeitssicherheit, Prozessoptimierung, Personalwesen und Technik
• Vorbereitung auf die eigenständige Steuerung eines operativen Bereichs als Area Manager:in
• Enge Zusammenarbeit mit einem internationalen Team innerhalb des europäischen Amazon-Netzwerks

A day in the life
Deine Betreuung im Programm
Du bist nicht allein. Während des gesamten Programms wirst du von zwei Seiten unterstützt:
• Dein:e Learning Manager:in am Standort begleitet dich durch alle drei Phasen, ist deine zentrale Ansprechperson und koordiniert deine Entwicklung
• Operative Führungskräfte mentoren dich während deiner Rotationen und geben dir direktes Feedback aus der Praxis
Zusätzlich bist du Teil einer deutschlandweiten Community dualer Student:innen - ein Netzwerk, das mit dir wächst.

________________________________________
Dein Alltag: Theorie und Praxis im Wochentakt
Das Studium läuft parallel zur Praxis - keine langen Blockphasen, sondern ein wöchentlicher Rhythmus:
• 2 Tage Studium an deinem IU-Standort (Logistik, Supply Chain, BWL, Personalführung)
• 2-3 Tage / 20 Stunden im Amazon Fulfillment Center oder Sort Center

Du bist kein Besucher im Betrieb. Du bist Teil des Teams - von Tag eins an.

Basic qualifications

- Allgemeine Hochschulreife, Fachhochschulreife / fachgebundene Hochschulreife
- Fließende Deutschkenntnisse in Wort und Schrift (C1-Niveau)
- Fortgeschrittene Englischkenntnisse in Wort und Schrift (B2-Niveau)
- Affinität für das Fach Mathematik
- Umgang mit MS-Office (insbesondere Kenntnisse in Excel, Word und PowerPoint)

Preferred qualifications

- Ausgeprägte Kommunikationsfähigkeit
- Eigeninitiative, Vorbildfunktion und „Hands-on-Mentalität"
- Interesse, Führungsverantwortung zu tragen

title: Principal Product Manager-Tech, eShop
descriptionHtml:
The Premium Shopping Experience team is on a mission to firmly establish Amazon as the premier destination for shopping high-quality premium products. We do this by intentionally surfacing contextually relevant premium selection to customers and elevating our shopping experiences and merchandising across the entire Store.

We are seeking a Product Manager to own the Traffic Drivers workstream — responsible for driving awareness, discovery, and engagement with premium selection through onsite and offsite marketing channels. This role sits at the intersection of marketing, merchandising, personalization, and customer experience, and is critical to converting existing customers into premium shoppers and increasing spend from existing premium customers.

Key job responsibilities
Own the traffic strategy for premium selection across onsite channels (Homepage, Browse Pages, Push Notifications, Email) and offsite channels (Paid Social, Display Ads, Creator Partnerships, Outbound Marketing), defining a steady drumbeat of campaigns that drive customer visits, product page views, and new-to-program acquisition.

Develop and execute the Homepage merchandising roadmap, including premium-focused campaigns, propensity-enabled widgets, and personalized collections that surface premium selection during evergreen periods and seasonal events.

Formalize the brand launch playbook for major premium brand launches, leveraging high-visibility channels and placements to maximize awareness and conversion.

Partner with the science team to leverage propensity models and brand classification signals to personalize traffic channel activities and curate cross-category premium collections.

Define and own traffic KPIs including customer visits, page views, new-to-program acquisition, and incremental revenue across all marketing and brand launch campaigns.

title: Creative Manager, éShop Content Services
descriptionHtml:
Elevated Shopping enhances the shopping experience through video, virtual production, photography, graphic design, and usability design. With a global network of Creative Hubs in North America, Europe, and Asia, Elevated Shopping focuses on video and CGI production, virtual production, fashion and product photography, photo retouching, graphic design, automated image acquisition, and image support services. We continuously innovate and set new industry standards for showcasing millions of products across multiple global marketplaces.

We are searching for a Creative Manager who will report to the Creative Hub Manager and lead end-to-end creative production for Amazon's London Creative Hub. This is a people manager role: the successful candidate will directly manage a team of Art Directors, Videographers, and creative professionals, owning their development, performance, and day-to-day direction. The Creative Manager will influence project management, coordinate with Producers on production schedules and budgets, and other stakeholders (who are cross-functional partners, not direct reports), and drive creative excellence across video, virtual production, photography, and motion content. This person must also have a strong understanding of generative AI tools and their application in creative workflows, as well as virtual production technologies.


Key job responsibilities
• Own end-to-end creative production across multiple brands and campaigns simultaneously from concept through to final delivery across stills, motion, and digital formats
• Define creative briefs and provide art direction to internal stakeholders and external brand partners, translating business objectives into compelling visual content
• Recommend production approaches and launch strategies based on performance data, client goals, and studio capabilities
• Directly manage Art Directors, Videographers, and creative professionals; partner with Producers, Digitechs, Stylists, Editors, and 3D Artists to ensure seamless cross-functional execution
• Drive timely decisions, clear blockers, and escalate appropriately to maintain momentum across concurrent productions
• Own resource allocation with Producers; balance creative ambition against operational constraints
• Ensure all creative output meets brand guidelines, platform specifications, and the studio's quality bar
• Optimise campaign workflows and team processes; recommend improvements to cross-team and partner processes
• Identify opportunities to improve production workflows including emerging tools (AI, virtual production) and pilot improvements within the team
• Own people management for direct reports including performance reviews, career development, coaching, and hiring; build a high-performing, creatively ambitious team culture



A day in the life
Your day begins with a scan of live production schedules and a quick check-in with your direct reports Art Directors, Stylists, Videographers to align on the day's priorities and clear any blockers before the studio floor gets busy. Mid-morning might see you leading a creative kick-off for a new video campaign, working through references and art direction with the team, before shifting into a storyboard or shot list review for a shoot already in motion. You'll stay closely connected with Producers throughout the day as a key stakeholder on timelines, resource allocation, and budget ensuring nothing slips between creative ambition and operational reality. By the afternoon, you're likely on set: overseeing a live video production, making real-time creative calls, and ensuring everything is captured to brief and to schedule. Alternatively, you might be in a post-production review session giving feedback on edits, grading, and pacing to bring a project over the line. The day closes with stakeholder updates, a 1:1 with a team member focused on development or creative growth, and forward-planning against the next production milestone.

About the team
Our Creative Hub team is a dynamic group of creative professionals spanning video production, photography, styling, virtual production, and post-production. We produce high-volume, high-quality visual content for global brands across fashion, beauty, lifestyle, and consumer electronics. We pride ourselves on operational excellence, creative innovation, and a collaborative culture that empowers every team member to deliver their best work.
