title: UX Designer II, Ops Tech Solution ACES
descriptionHtml:
Do you believe great design is how technology make sense? Are you energized by a studio where UX design is the thread that ties everything together? Interested in creating a single visual system carries across video, animation, interactive 3D, and the knowledge articles people actually read, and where the design decisions you make are tested against real user data?

We are looking for an UX Designer to join Ops Tech Solutions (OTS) ACES team supporting the IT For Me high-output creative studio in Nashville, TN. IT For Me makes technology easier to understand and solutions easier to find. We do it with a deliberate visual framework, a consistent style and interaction pattern that carries across every medium we deliver: from self-service tech videos to interactive 3D hardware guides, redesigned knowledge-base articles, and live events. Our work is not decoration. We design how information is received, measure whether it lands, and iterate to improve it.

This is an experienced UX role on the team. You will own the steady, high-volume work that keeps the studio moving, and you will do it as a designer producing within our visual framework, redesigning knowledge content so it is clearer and easier to use, and helping gather the feedback and usage data that tells us what is working. All while collaborating with senior designers on the most complex, high-end builds. The through-line in everything you make is the IT For Me design system, and your job is to apply it, keep it consistent, and help it improve.

If you are strong creative in the visual design space, curious about how users respond to what you make, organized enough to run a studio, and eager to be challenged within systems-level UX work, motion, and 3D, we want to meet you.

Key job responsibilities
You will own the foundational, high-frequency design and production work that keeps OTS ACES delivering at pace, and you will grow the UX craft by:
• Apply the design system consistently across every deliverable (lower thirds, titles, intros, thumbnails, article layouts, and graphics) so the experience is coherent whatever the medium.
• Partner with senior designers and technical stakeholders to take briefs from intake to delivery, articulate the reasoning behind a design choice, and keep SIM tickets and worklogs current.
• Helping gather and interpret design feedback and usage data: article view and deflection metrics, A/B comparisons, and user or stakeholder feedback, then use what you learn to refine the work and inform the next iteration.
• Build supporting motion and graphic assets in After Effects, Illustrator, Photoshop, and contribute to interactive 3D hardware guides, growing into more advanced motion and 3D work over time.
• Own studio equipment and inventory: track, maintain, and stage cameras, lenses, lighting, audio gear, and accessories so the kit is always shoot-ready, and flag repairs or purchasing needs.
• Produce and edit the studio’s steady-state video content, including interview videos, leadership and PR-style announcement videos, edited in Adobe Premiere Pro and After Effects.


A day in the life
The OTS ACES day is varied and driven by our customers. UX design here is a full loop, not a hand-off. We study how our content is received, through usage data, A/B studies, and direct feedback, and we use that evidence to improve the design and to explain to stakeholders why a given approach works.
You might start working within a knowledge article within our framework and checking last week’s view and deflection numbers to see how a recent redesign is performing, spend the rest of the day in the studio running cameras and audio for a shoot.


About the team
IT For Me is the UX and creative studio within OTS ACES. We produce high-quality, visual-driven content that makes tech easier to understand and solutions easier to find across video, animation, interactive 3D hardware guides, knowledge-base articles, and live events. What ties it all together is a single, deliberate design system: one visual language and interaction pattern, delivered across many mediums. We design with evidence, measuring how our work is received and iterating on it, while insisting on high standards and moving fast with care about the work that reflects our culture of innovation, inclusion, and excellence.

Basic qualifications

- 3+ years of design experience
- Have an online portfolio or samples of work on resume, demonstrating experience creating great end-to-end, user-centered design solutions and patterns, across desktop and mobile devices
- Knowledge of and proficiency in a variety of design tools such as Photoshop, Illustrator, Fireworks, and InDesign

Preferred qualifications

- Experience planning and executing effective customer research, solo, or in partnership with a UX Researcher
- Knowledge of Adobe Creative software, primarily Premiere, After Effects, Photoshop/Indesign at an advanced level
- Experience with one or more of the following industry tools: 3D Studio Max, Maya, Photoshop, Zbrush, Substance, Unreal, Blender, etc
- Experience in HTML, CSS, or JavaScript

title: Data Center Chief Engineer, Data Center Engineering Operation
descriptionHtml:
As Chief Engineer, you will be responsible for ensuring that all electrical, mechanical, and fire/life safety equipment within the data center is operating at peak efficiency. This involves planned preventative maintenance of equipment, daily corrective work, and emergency response. You are expected to be a singular focal point for all facility operations and to support Amazon within its owned and operated data centers.

You should be able to manage large scale impacting projects and new region support from conception to completion. These projects involve large amounts of independent work as well as collaboration with external support groups including engineering, automation, procurement, and finance in both local and global settings. As Chief Engineer, you will be tasked with creating and delivering on key milestones, obtaining and tracking quotes for all necessary costs, and documenting project results for future implementation at other facilities. The goals of such projects are for the Chief Engineers to drive innovation and resiliency while reducing operational costs in the facilities.

AWS Infrastructure Services (AIS)

AWS Infrastructure Services owns the design, planning, delivery, and operation of all AWS global infrastructure. In other words, we’re the people who keep the cloud running. We support all AWS data centers and all of the servers, storage, networking, power, and cooling equipment that ensure our customers have continual access to the innovation they rely on. We work on the most challenging problems, with thousands of variables impacting the supply chain — and we’re looking for talented people who want to help.

You’ll join a diverse team of software, hardware, and network engineers, supply chain specialists, security experts, operations managers, and other vital roles. You’ll collaborate with people across AWS to help us deliver the highest standards for safety and security while providing seemingly infinite capacity at the lowest possible cost for our customers. And you’ll experience an inclusive culture that welcomes bold ideas and empowers you to own them to completion.

The Worldwide Sustainability (WWS) organization capitalizes on Amazon’s scale, speed, ability to build, invent, and simplify a resilient and sustainable company. We manage our social and environmental impacts globally, and drive solutions that enable our customers, businesses, and the world to become more sustainable.


Key job responsibilities
• Train and support the Engineering team in their role of providing electrical and mechanical equipment troubleshooting and operations
• Implement and execute site or equipment-specific training exercises. Exercises cover, but are not limited to: stand-by diesel generators, switchgear, UPSs, PDUs, AHUs, chillers etc.
• Oversee day-to-day operation and maintenance of mechanical and electrical equipment in data center sites
• Operate independently, with limited direct management
• Assist in the design and build-out of new facilities and perform root cause analysis of equipment failures
• Act as an escalation point for all facilities-related issues within the data center region. Work OT hours as needed to support site stability
• Troubleshoot and report facility and data sever-level events within internal Service Level Agreements (SLA)
• Create and deploy standard practices for Engineering Operations Technicians, Chief Engineers, and vendor support teams
• Ensure all safety procedures are adhered to by vendors, and AWS staff

PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS
• Work at height, and from ladders
• Perform physical tasks during the shift
• Work in a noisy environment, with ear protection

A day in the life
- Working semi-autonomously in operation and maintenance of mechanical and electrical equipment in a data center
- Execution of project scopes of basic complexity
- Providing timely escalation for all facilities-related issues within the data center
- First-line troubleshooting and reporting of facility and high-criticality events
- Providing assistance to junior and peer EOTs
- Oversight of third-party vendors to ensure that all work performed is in accordance with established safety protocols, best practices, and local legislation
- Utilization of administrative tools for change management, ticketing, and asset management.

About the team
Diverse Experiences
Amazon values diverse experiences. Even if you do not meet all of the preferred qualifications and skills listed in the job description, we encourage candidates to apply. If your career is just starting, hasn’t followed a traditional path, or includes alternative experiences, don’t let it stop you from applying.

Why AWS
Amazon Web Services (AWS) is the world’s most comprehensive and broadly adopted cloud platform. We pioneered cloud computing and never stopped innovating — that’s why customers from the most successful startups to Global 500 companies trust our robust suite of products and services to power their businesses.

We value work-life harmony. Achieving success at work should never come at the expense of sacrifices at home, which is why we strive for flexibility as part of our working culture. When we feel supported in the workplace and at home, there’s nothing we can’t achieve.

Our inclusion events foster stronger, more collaborative teams. Our continual innovation is fueled by the bold ideas, fresh perspectives, and passionate voices our teams bring to everything we do.

title: Product Growth Manager, Amazon Credit - Brazil, Amazon Payments
descriptionHtml:
Amazon is the world's largest e-commerce and cloud computing company, serving hundreds of millions of customers across 20+ countries and reshaping how people shop, pay, and access financial services. Amazon Payment Products BR has the mission to launch and manage payments products that will drive affinity and affordability to our customers. Amazon Crédito is Amazon's first-party lending product in Brazil, offering credit solutions directly to customers on our platform.

This role oversee the growth strategy, product roadmap, and P&L performance for Amazon Crédito. The successful candidate will combine deep business acumen with analytical rigor to drive measurable improvements not only through incremental funnel optimization, but through leap growth opportunities, strategic partnerships, structural changes to the business model, cost structure transformation and new revenue streams that fundamentally change the trajectory of the product. This requires someone who thinks like a business owner: fluent in P&L dynamics, able to identify where margin is created or destroyed, and capable of building conviction around bold bets while managing risk. The ideal candidate is a self-starter who thrives in ambiguous, fast-paced environments, someone who can go deep on data to identify root causes and growth opportunities, then shift to managing complex stakeholder landscapes, coordinating with external partners (BaaS providers, fund managers and administrators, credit bureaus, regulatory bodies) and internal teams (Product, Marketing, Engineering, Finance, Risk, and Legal), to drive solutions from problem identification through launch and impact measurement.

Key job responsibilities
- Growth Strategy & Business Ownership: Define and execute the growth plan for Amazon Crédito across the full customer lifecycle. Go beyond base optimization: identify and pursue leap growth opportunities through strategic partnerships, new distribution channels, product adjacencies, and structural changes to the business model that step-change the product's trajectory.

- P&L & Margin Optimization: analyze revenue drivers, cost structure, and margin levers to identify opportunities for profitable growth. Develop a clear view of unit economics across customer segments. Translate P&L insights into strategic priorities, knowing when to invest for growth and when to optimize for efficiency.

- Cost Structure Transformation: Identify and quantify cost reduction opportunities across the funnel, customer acquisition cost, servicing cost, cost of risk, funding cost and partner with relevant teams to execute. Propose structural alternatives and build business cases that balance short-term savings with long-term scalability.

- Funnel Optimization & Experimentation: Build and manage the experimentation roadmap: design, execute, and analyze A/B tests and multivariate experiments to optimize conversion rates, credit adoption, and repayment behavior at every stage

- Strategic Partnerships & Stakeholder Management Identify, evaluate, and structure partnerships that unlock new customer segments, reduce costs, or create competitive advantages. Coordinate with external partners and internal cross-functional teams to align on shared success criteria and navigate the regulatory landscape of consumer lending in Brazil.

- Metrics, Analytical Rigor & Operational Excellence Develop deep expertise in lending growth KPIs (eligible-to-enrolled conversion, activation rates, utilization, delinquency-adjusted retention). Lead daily operations with discipline — assess risks, monitor progress with actionable insights, and resolve bottlenecks to keep initiatives on track.

- Experience in product, program, or project management in leading cross-functional teams in delivery of major new products or services
- Experience managing technical products or online services
- Experience in product or program management, product marketing, business development or technology
- Speak, write, and read fluently in English

Preferred qualifications

- Experience driving new business segment or services launches

descriptionHtml:
【職務内容】
Amazonは「 地球上で最もお客様を大切にし、地球上で最も豊富な品揃え」というビジョンを目指しています。このビジョンを実現するために、素晴らしい仲間を求めています。オーナーシップを持ち変化と革新に情熱を持って取り組む方を求めています。
我々はカスタマーエクスペリエンスを向上させるために進歩し続けています。我々の企業DNAとしてイノベーションと創造があります。皆さんにその力を発揮して頂き、日々発生する問題に工夫を凝らしシンプルな方法で解決し、これからのAmazonを一緒に作り上げ、Amazonと共に未来を歩みましょう。

【業務概要】
Amazonは配送拠点で働くIT Support Engineerの応募をお待ちしております。日本のFCでは何百万点もの商品を取り揃えており、毎日世界中に配送しています。まずはFCの中の“物の流れ” を知って頂きます。その後、ITの観点から変更や改善を行って頂くようになります。ITインフラを運用し、FC内の全てのITインフラが問題なく安定的に稼働している事が求められます。Amazonでは一日として同じ日はありません。多くの変化と多様な環境の中で活躍して頂きます。

· 成長の機会 – Amazonの最先端のインフラに携わる重要な運用ポジションです。最新技術から現場の継続的な改善まで。我々の業務には運用といえどもイノベーションが不可欠です

例）9:00-18:00, 8:00-17:00, 12:00-21:00等

【Job Description】
Amazon is aiming for a "vision of being the Earth's most customer-centric company and having the Earth's biggest selection." To realize this vision, we are seeking wonderful colleagues. We are looking for people who have a sense of ownership, and who are passionate about change and innovation.
We continue to progress to improve the customer experience. Innovation and creativity are part of our corporate DNA. We want you to demonstrate this power, come up with ingenious solutions to daily problems in simple ways, and help build the future of Amazon together with us.

【Job Summary】
Amazon is now accepting applications for IT Support Engineers to work at our fulfillment centers. Our Japan FCs store millions of products and ship them worldwide every day. First, you will learn about the "flow of goods" within the FC. Afterward, you will be responsible for making changes and improvements from an IT perspective. You will be required to operate the IT infrastructure to ensure that all IT infrastructure within the FC is running stably and without issues. At Amazon, no two days are the same. You will thrive in an environment of constant change and diversity.
Diversity is one of the key elements necessary for enhancing teamwork. age, nationality, and experience do not matter. We are looking for colleagues with diverse backgrounds and experiences to work together.

【What kind of experience can you gain?】
Growth opportunities - This is an important operational position involving Amazon's infrastructure. From the latest technologies to ongoing improvements in the field, innovation is essential in our work, even in operations.
The fulfillment center network is expanding at a very rapid pace. You will take on many challenges and complex problems, and work to further expand our services to meet customer demand.

OTS Field IT

【Career Path】
We actively promote career advancement, and you will have the opportunity to take on various career challenges both within and outside the department. In addition to senior support engineers, there are positions such as engineering leaders and IT managers in the personnel management and management fields. Outside the department, many members have also taken on challenges in remote support, procurement/materials management, and technology development departments.

There are detailed training and OJT programs for new hires, and a wealth of documents and learning content necessary for the work. At Amazon, the mindset is that everyone, including colleagues and related departments, are customers. There is a culture of supporting each other when someone is struggling or facing a difficult problem. The company has a mentoring system and exchanges between different sites, creating a supportive environment where you can work with peace of mind.

title: Responsable Sécurité au Travail, Workplace Health and Safety
descriptionHtml:
Chez Amazon, nous avons besoin de personnes talentueuses et expérimentées pour nous aider à travailler de manière sûre et efficace. En tant que Responsable Workplace Health and Safety (WHS), votre rôle est essentiel pour impulser des améliorations sur site et au niveau régional. Vous dirigerez votre équipe et aiderez vos collègues à maintenir des normes élevées, tout en favorisant une culture de sécurité et d'inclusion sur vos sites.

Key job responsibilities
Gérer votre équipe sur site, tout en collaborant régulièrement avec d'autres équipes au sein de l'entreprise. Utiliser les outils de reporting internes pour analyser les rapports de données et les causes profondes afin d'aider la direction à prendre des décisions en matière de sécurité. Proposer des directives et des dispositions pour les projets et les politiques de santé et de sécurité. Piloter les programmes conçus pour améliorer la culture de la sécurité chez Amazon.

A day in the life
Ce poste extrêmement varié sera basé sur l'un de nos sites et vous permettra de contribuer directement à de nombreux aspects de notre culture de sécurité. Vous gérerez les normes de santé et de sécurité tout en améliorant le fonctionnement et l'efficacité. Vous dirigerez également votre équipe et l'aiderez à mettre en œuvre les changements en réponse aux retours des collaborateurs ou à saisir les opportunités d'amélioration continue des processus.

About the team
L'équipe Workplace Health and Safety (WHS) joue un rôle essentiel pour garantir le bien-être mental et physique de nos collaborateurs au travail. Notre équipe travaille avec les responsables, les associés et les administrations locales sur l'ensemble de nos sites, en assurant le respect des politiques d'Amazon et des réglementations légales, et en garantissant la sécurité de nos environnements de travail. L'équipe offre une variété d'opportunités, des Techniciens de Sécurité aux Responsables de Programmes. Quel que soit votre poste, vous contribuerez au développement et à la mise en œuvre de la stratégie de sécurité sur l'ensemble du réseau.

Basic qualifications

- BUT (Licence) en Hygiène, Sécurité et Environnement, ou qualification équivalente conforme au Cadre Européen des Certifications (CEC/EQF) dans un domaine lié à la santé et sécurité.
- Connaissance de la législation française en matière de santé et sécurité au travail.
- Expérience pertinente dans la gestion d'une équipe.
- Maîtrise du français et bonne connaissance de l'anglais (B2), à l'écrit et à l'oral.

Preferred qualifications

- Les qualifications préférées ne sont pas requises pour postuler chez Amazon. Si vous possédez toutes les qualifications de base ci-dessus, nous serions ravis de recevoir votre candidature.
- Expérience avec les méthodologies Lean, 5S ou Kaizen.
- Expérience dans la planification ou la gestion d'initiatives écoresponsables.
- Adhésion à un organisme professionnel dans le domaine de la santé et sécurité au travail.
- Expérience dans la gestion et la communication avec un large éventail de parties prenantes, y compris vos pairs, vos collaborateurs et la direction.

Amazon est un employeur engagé pour l'égalité des chances. Nous sommes convaincus qu'une main d'oeuvre diversifée est essentielle à notre réussite. Nous prenons nos décisions de recrutement en fonction de votre expérience et de vos compétences. Nous apprécions votre envie de découvrir, d'inventer, de simplifier et de construire. La protection de votre vie privée et la sécurité de vos données constituent depuis longtemps une priorité absolue pour Amazon. Veuillez consulter notre Politique de Confidentialité pour en savoir plus sur la façon dont nous collectons, utilisons et traitons les données personnelles de nos candidats.

title: Software Development Engineer II, EC2 Blackfoot Peering Team
descriptionHtml:
AWS Infrastructure Services owns the design, planning, delivery, and operation of all AWS global infrastructure. In other words, we’re the people who keep the cloud running. We support all AWS data centers and all of the servers, storage, networking, power, and cooling equipment that ensure our customers have continual access to the innovation they rely on. We work on the most challenging problems, with thousands of variables impacting the supply chain — and we’re looking for talented people who want to help.

You’ll join a diverse team of software, hardware, and network engineers, supply chain specialists, security experts, operations managers, and other vital roles. You’ll collaborate with people across AWS to help us deliver the highest standards for safety and security while providing seemingly infinite capacity at the lowest possible cost for our customers. And you’ll experience an inclusive culture that welcomes bold ideas and empowers you to own them to completion.

Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (EC2) Networking is looking for a Software Development Engineer II to help build forwarding and encapsulation services that power large-scale networking within AWS. Your work will directly impact millions of customers who rely on EC2 every day.

We are growing fast and looking for kernel and embedded C programmers who can deliver ultra-high performance. Our goal is to process many millions of packets per second on embedded CPU cores. This requires implementing highly optimized data structures and low-level tuning to our hardware. If you have strong experience in C or C++ and a passion for systems software engineering such as kernel or embedded development, this is a unique opportunity to join us in building the platform that will underpin all new EC2 Virtual Private Cloud features in the years to come.

Dataplane engineers work on a lower level of the software stack that directly interacts with hardware. They require knowledge of programming languages optimized for lower-level work such as C, C++, Rust, and Assembly Language, along with the ability to read a hardware specification for a network card and optimize code to run on it.

Key job responsibilities
- Design and implement high-performance forwarding and encapsulation services in C and C++, optimizing data structures and tuning code for embedded CPU cores processing millions of packets per second.
- Collaborate with hardware and software engineers across EC2 Networking to translate hardware specifications into performant dataplane code, ensuring scalability and reliability for AWS customers.
- Participate in architecture decisions, design reviews, and code reviews, providing meaningful feedback to teammates and mentoring junior engineers on best practices for low-level systems development.
Own features across the full development lifecycle — from scoping and design through implementation, testing, deployment, and operations — while identifying root causes of operational issues and driving permanent fixes.

A day in the life
You might start your morning investigating a performance regression on a new network card, profiling packet-processing paths to find the bottleneck. After a design review with your team, you could spend the afternoon writing and testing optimized C code for a new encapsulation feature. You will regularly sync with hardware engineers and partner teams across EC2 to align on upcoming card capabilities and feature requirements, balancing hands-on coding with collaborative planning.

About the team
Our team is dedicated to supporting new members. We have a broad mix of experience levels and Amazon tenures, and we are building an environment that celebrates knowledge sharing and mentorship. Senior engineers on the team enjoy mentoring through one-on-one sessions and thorough, kind code reviews. We assign projects based on what will help each engineer develop new skills and take on greater challenges over time. With access to Principal and Distinguished Engineers across EC2 and AWS, there are many opportunities to grow.

Basic qualifications

- 3+ years of non-internship professional software development experience
- 2+ years of non-internship design or architecture (design patterns, reliability and scaling) of new and existing systems experience
- 1+ years of software development engineer or related occupational experience
- 1+ years of designing and developing large-scale, multi-tiered, multi-threaded, embedded or distributed software applications, tools, systems, and services using: C#, C++, Java, or Perl experience
- 1+ years of Object Oriented Design experience
- Bachelor's degree or foreign equivalent in Computer Science, Engineering, Mathematics, or a related field
- Experience programming with at least one software programming language

Preferred qualifications

- 3+ years of full software development life cycle, including coding standards, code reviews, source control management, build processes, testing, and operations experience
- Bachelor's degree in computer science or equivalent

title: Senior Reliability Maintenance Engineering Technician, RME
descriptionHtml:
Our Reliability Maintenance Engineering (RME) team is central to Amazon's commitment to innovation. As Amazon evolves and adapts, this team makes sure that the tools and technologies we use do as well. As a Senior RME Technician, you'll help us stay one step ahead, adopting the latest technologies and identifying new and efficient ways of working. In this role, you’ll pay close attention to our processes to help maintain our high standards, and you’ll put in place upgrades to take that standard even higher.

Key job responsibilities
• Demonstrate best practice on using equipment safely and monitor teams to ensure everyone follows the correct processes
• Keep track of equipment performance through visual checks, condition-based monitoring, and preventative maintenance tasks and schedule additional servicing when required
• Supervise technicians on shift to support their development and act as the first point of contact for Reliability Maintenance Engineers
• Solve issues in equipment to reduce downtime for operations so they can process packages as quickly as possible
• Support in finding ways to continually improve systems and standardise processes across the EU network


A day in the life
In every shift, you’ll be leading a team to make sure everyone has the equipment they need and that it’s running properly. That involves monitoring processes so that regulations and policies are followed and ensuring that preventative maintenance is carried out to increase equipment uptime.

With everything you observe on your shifts, you’ll suggest improvements to make our systems more efficient and productive and then implement those improvements across an EU-wide function. You’ll also be monitoring processes with tools like Scada to guarantee their performance, as well as working closely with your line manager to assist with admin tasks.

This role is located at one of our operational sites. You’ll work shift patterns, which may include some weekends and nights. As you develop your experience within this exciting part of Amazon, you’ll be well-placed to progress into more senior roles.

About the team
Our Reliability Maintenance Engineering or RME team keep our equipment performing at its best. We're a technically minded team, made up of excellent team players and guided by experienced leaders. We work together to maintain, troubleshoot and repair equipment across our global network of fulfilment centres. descriptionHtml:

About the role
Global energy demand will rise sharply over the coming decades, and the power and utilities sector is racing to modernize the grid, decarbonize, electrify transport, and meet power demand not seen in generations. AWS is investing billions in generation and delivery to power sustainable data center growth and is reinventing energy workflows with AI and the cloud. You will own the EMEA partnership portfolio end-to-end with the region's largest and most strategically significant P&U relationships carrying multi-year portfolio responsibility rather than a single account. You will Think Big where there is no playbook, structuring first-of-their-kind agreements and novel commercial models in markets where AWS's position is still forming and make high-judgment calls with incomplete information (Are Right, A Lot). You will Earn Trust as the advisor of choice to energy-industry CxOs, close the region's largest multi-party agreements, and act as a force multiplier who raises the bar across the BD team through mentorship, reusable playbooks, and visible thought leadership (Hire and Develop the Best, Invent and Simplify).

• Structure and close the region's largest strategic agreements encompassing a confluence of commitments to technology, infrastructure, and AI with major EMEA energy customers.
• Serve as strategic advisor to customer executives (CEO, CFO, CIO, CTO, VP), building trusted relationships that span infrastructure partnerships and enterprise cloud and AI adoption.
• Act as the managed gateway between EMEA account teams and AWS Infrastructure and power-procurement teams, coordinating and elevating commercial power discussions.
• Orchestrate a pan-Amazon network (Retail, Prime, Transportation, Fulfillment, Data Center Infrastructure, Amazon Business, Sustainability) into EMEA engagements as inputs to strategic agreement value propositions.

title: Principal Product Manager, Shipping Express, Amazon Air Cargo
descriptionHtml:
You're a Principal Product Manager with deep experience in supply chain, transportation, or logistics product strategy within complex, rapidly scaling organizations. You've owned end-to-end product vision for a shipping, delivery, or transportation product at scale, and you have a track record of turning operational networks into differentiated, customer-facing products that customers love and adopt to. You excel where the problem spans network operations, product definition, commercial strategy, and customer experience — and you bring the strategic judgment to define the right long-term bets while delivering near-term value.

You have strong analytical skills and are comfortable diving deep into transit-time and cutoff economics, network flow and injection constraints, coverage and lane profitability, pricing structure, and competitive benchmarking to decide where product and network investment drives outsized revenue and share impact. You understand that this is not project management — this is setting direction for a shipping product that competes head-to-head with industry leading services and must earn every shipper's choice.

High judgment is expected at the Principal bar: defining the product promise and service bar customer-back (not operations-forward), making trade-offs between operational feasibility and customer delight, deciding when to build versus influence a platform or operations team's roadmap, and influencing across operations, network design, commercial, finance, and engineering teams without direct authority. You set strategy that other senior leaders and teams align to, you regularly engage with senior leadership to secure investment and drive high-stakes decisions, and you are relied on to be right a lot. You have a proven track record of building a transportation or delivery product that became a durable competitive advantage.

Key job responsibilities
Strategic Product Management — Define the executive-level vision for the Shipping Express 2-day product and translate it into actionable multi-year roadmaps aligned across operations, network design, product, commercial, and engineering. Define the product customer-back — product promise, cutoff times, guaranteed delivery windows, tracking/visibility SLAs, pickup experience, coverage footprint, service tiers, and pricing framework — benchmarked dimension by dimension against UPS 2nd Day Air and FedEx 2Day. Own end-to-end outcomes and business impact (shipper acquisition and retention, volume and share growth, delivery-performance SLAs, cost per shipment, and shipper satisfaction).

End-to-End Product Lifecycle & Quality Ownership — Own the full product cycle for Shipping Express and the quality of the product at every stage:

Vision — Set the long-term product vision and the "why now," grounded in customer need and competitive gap.
Requirements — Translate the vision into clear, prioritized product requirements that engineering and operations can build from.
Phased launch — Launch in deliberate phases (pilot → scale → expand), defining the entry and exit criteria for each phase rather than attempting a single big-bang release.
Measurement — Instrument the product and define the success metrics up front; measure actual performance against the product promise and the business case after each phase.
Quality improvement — Identify quality gaps from the data (service misses, exceptions, defects, failure modes) and drive the highest-impact improvements back into the product and network.
Product evolution — Continuously evolve the roadmap based on customer feedback, operational quality and cost, and P&L outcomes — deciding what to double down on, what to fix, and what to retire.
Cross-Team & Network Leadership — Lead product vision and execution across multi-org dependencies, driving alignment across network design, sort/injection operations, air gateway capacity, and middle-mile/last-mile execution. Translate hard operational constraints (pickup-to-injection timing, gateway cutoffs, sort-center flow) into a single recommended network path and a product customers can rely on. Eliminate fragmented ownership and missed handoffs across the shipping journey; own the build-vs-influence calls and ensure capabilities land in the right long-term home.

Operational Excellence & Scale — Design a product and the supporting network capabilities that scale with volume growth without proportional increases in manual exception handling. Use data to identify and eliminate the highest-impact friction points across the pickup-to-delivery experience and the lanes that drive cost and service risk. Build the governance and review mechanisms that keep cross-org investment aligned year over year.

A day in the life
Set the strategic direction for the Shipping Express product across teams — aligning operations, commercial, and engineering around a single customer-back product definition, not a stack of operational compromises.
Deep dive into data (transit-time and on-time performance, cutoff and injection constraints, lane profitability, competitive benchmarks, shipper feedback) to shape the roadmap and decide where to invest for maximum share and margin impact.
Run the product cycle end to end — move initiatives from vision to requirements to phased launch, then measure outcomes, surface quality gaps, and feed them back into the next iteration.
Partner with engineering and operations leaders to shape network and product design, ensuring the product scales with volume growth and holds its service promise.
Unblock cross-org dependencies before they become escalations; frame program narratives for senior leadership — connecting network and product progress to business outcomes.
Spend time with Ops teams and in the network to pressure-test whether the product performs for shippers in the real world.

What this takes

Someone who toggles between deep product and operational insight and strategic product leadership — owning the full product cycle from vision through launch, measurement, and continuous quality improvement — and turning a complex transportation network into a scalable, benchmark-beating 2-day shipping product that shippers choose.

Basic qualifications

- 10+ years of product or program management, product marketing, business development or technology experience
- 10+ years of blending product and program management skills to execute strategic initiatives about process creation, standardization, and improvement experience
- Bachelor's degree
- Experience owning/driving roadmap strategy and definition
- Experience with end to end product delivery
- Experience with feature delivery and tradeoffs of a product
- Experience as a product manager or owner

Preferred qualifications

- Experience owning technology products

title: Data Scientist, CloudTune
descriptionHtml:
Amazon's eCommerce Foundation (eCF) organization provides the core technologies that drive and power Amazon's Stores, Digital, and Other (SDO) businesses. Millions of customer page views and orders per day are enabled by the systems eCF builds from the ground up. CloudTune, within eCF, empowers growth and business agility needs by automatically and efficiently managing AWS capacity and business processes needed to safely meet Amazon's customer demand. CloudTune serves its primary customers, internal software teams, through forecast-driven automation of cost controllership, capacity management, and scaling. We predict expected load, and drive procurement and allocation of AWS capacity for new product launches and high-velocity events like Prime Day and Cyber Monday.

CloudTune is looking for a Data Scientist to join our forecasting and optimization team. The team develops sophisticated algorithms that combine machine learning-based demand forecasting with mathematical optimization to solve large-scale capacity planning problems under uncertainty. We work with massive datasets — spanning thousands of availability zone and instance family combinations across global regions — to determine optimal resource allocation strategies that balance infrastructure holding costs against service availability requirements. These models directly inform multi-million dollar capacity investment decisions and drive automated procurement, retention, and release policies across Amazon's compute infrastructure.

As a Data Scientist in CloudTune, you will work with other scientists, software engineers, data engineers, and product managers on a variety of important research problems in the areas of stochastic optimization, time series modeling, and operations research. You will work on statistical problems with a high level of ambiguity. You will analyze and process large amounts of data, develop new algorithms and improve existing approaches based on statistical models, machine learning algorithms and big data solutions to automatically scale Amazon’s compute infrastructure, optimizing the balance between availability risk and cost efficiency for all of Amazon businesses.

Key job responsibilities
- Process and analyze large data sets, mining additional data sources as needed
- Build statistical models and drive scalable solutions for multi-year capacity demand forecasting horizons
- Create, enhance, and maintain technical documentation, and present to other scientists and business leaders
- Process and analyze large-scale operational data to identify patterns and inform model development
- Create, enhance, and maintain technical documentation, and present research findings to scientists, engineering teams, and senior leadership

Basic qualifications

- 2+ years of data scientist experience
- 3+ years of data querying languages (e.g. SQL), scripting languages (e.g. Python) or statistical/mathematical software (e.g. R, SAS, Matlab, etc.) experience
- 3+ years of machine learning/statistical modeling data analysis tools and techniques, and parameters that affect their performance experience
- 1+ years of working with or evaluating AI systems experience
- Experience applying quantitative analysis to solve business problems and making data-driven business decisions
- Knowledge of machine learning concepts and their application to reasoning and problem-solving
- Currently has, or is in the process of obtaining, a Master's degree or above in Science, Technology, Engineering, or Mathematics (STEM)

Preferred qualifications

- Ph.D. in Science, Technology, Engineering, or Mathematics (STEM)
- Experience in a ML or data scientist role with a large technology company
- Experience in defining and creating benchmarks for assessing GenAI model performance
- Experience effectively communicating complex concepts through written and verbal communication
- Knowledge of relevant statistical measures such as confidence intervals, significance of error measurements, development and evaluation data sets, etc.

title: Strategic Sourcing Manager (Indirect), Global Corporate Procurement
descriptionHtml:
At Amazon, our vision is to be Earth's most customer-centric company. Our passion for invention leads us to pioneer and globalize new businesses and customer offerings daily. As we rapidly become the world's largest consumer of corporate services in many categories, the Corporate Strategic Procurement team is seeking a Strategic Sourcing Manager to join our team. This role is uniquely positioned at the nexus of business units across Amazon, and offers singular vision into a broad spectrum of cross-company initiatives and strategies on a global scale. Using this unique insight, the Strategic Sourcing Manager will build and lead sourcing engagements for both existing and newly emerging categories of spend, as well as negotiate multi-faceted partnership agreements for Amazon's high-growth businesses worldwide. Strategic Sourcing Managers own complex categories across multiple business units and regions, often in markets with limited competition and pricing transparency, and lead transformational sourcing initiatives with global scope. Strategic Sourcing Managers are expert practitioners in creating competitive environments, and have a strong bias for decisionmaking rooted in data and analytics. They routinely influence C-level vendor relationships by advising senior Amazon leaders across multiple stakeholder groups on the direction of sourcing projects in support of business unit and corporate goals, and they raise the bar for sourcing peers across the global team. Successful candidates must work well in a fast-paced and often ambiguous arena, and will be rewarded by working alongside highly collaborative and entrepreneurial colleagues in an environment that feels much more "startup" than "big company". Spend categories under management include indirect categories such as Logistics, Technology, such as Software, Hardware, Data Purchase, Telecommunication, Cybersecurity, among others. If you are an experienced sourcing professional with a passion for serving customers and for driving change and impact on a global scale, then we would love to talk with you.

Key job responsibilities
Owning one or more complex (sub-)categories across multiple business units and/or regions, developing and executing (sub-)category strategies
Developing global sourcing strategies to deliver against business objectives for internal clients, and achieving sustainable relationships with suppliers.
Managing categories in markets with limited competition and limited pricing transparency, proactively identifying and mitigating supplier, commercial, and ESG risk.
Evaluating supplier core competencies and competitive positioning using industry cost models and bench-marking analysis.
Managing the fundamentals of sourcing and supplier engagement activities, including RFx, spend pattern analysis, contract analysis, bid evaluation, negotiations, and supplier consolidation.
Leading transformational sourcing projects with complex, global scope, coordinating work across team members and regions.
Working with business and finance leaders to identify and drive savings and controllership improvements, focusing on total cost of ownership, and value creation beyond cost savings.
Presenting sourcing strategies, recommendations, and decisions to senior leaders up to three levels above you.
Contributing inputs to annual and long-range operating plans (OP1, OP2, and three-year forecast).
Providing guidance to internal stakeholders on procurement processes and maintaining procurement ethics in accordance with Amazon's global policies.
Preparing and holding business reviews with stakeholders to review vendor performance, future opportunities, and/or challenges.
Mentoring and sharing best practices with sourcing peers across the global team.


A day in the life
Your morning might start with a cross-functional alignment call for an upcoming RFP involving three business units, followed by analyzing bid responses and building a recommendation deck for senior leadership. After lunch, you're on a negotiation call with a strategic supplier's C-suite to finalize contract terms, then pivoting to a spend review with Finance to validate savings actuals against targets. You'll close the day by coaching a business partner through the supplier evaluation framework for an upcoming engagement. No two days look the same — you'll balance long-range strategic planning with hands-on execution, often managing five or more active sourcing engagements simultaneously across different stages of the lifecycle.





About the team
Global Corporate Procurement (GCP) manages Amazon's indirect spend across Employee Services, Marketing, Professional Services, Technology, Logistics, and Real Estate & Facilities. We're a global team of sourcing professionals who combine analytical rigor with creative problem-solving to deliver sustainable value at scale. Our culture values deep ownership, intellectual curiosity, and a bias for action — we move fast, but we move smart. You'll be joining a team where your work is visible to senior leadership and directly tied to Amazon's bottom line.

Basic qualifications

- Experience with practicing best-in-class procurement processes (category management, benchmarking, should-cost models, RFX, reverse auction, contracting, etc.)
- 5+ years of relevant strategic sourcing and category management in categories such as logistics, professional services, support or maintenance spend, supply chain, forecasting, manufacturing, sourcing/procurement, or vendor management experience
- Experience managing spend categories that include three or more of the following: Logistics, IT Software, IT
- Services, Corporate Services, Marketing, Contingent labor, Facilities and Real estate, Capital Expenditure and Tail Spend (Indirect Categories)

Preferred qualifications

- Bachelor's degree or equivalent
- Experience in a non-mandated, indirect procurement function at a multinational corporation
- Experience owning complex sourcing categories across multiple business units and/or regions
- Experience managing categories in markets with limited competition or limited pricing transparency, including proactive supplier risk management
- Experience leading transformational or cross-regional sourcing initiatives with global scope
- Experience advising and presenting sourcing strategy to senior executives and influencing C-level vendor relationships
- Experience contributing to annual or long-range operating plans
- Experience mentoring peers or coordinating sourcing work across a distributed team

title: Technical Program Manager,  Availability Serviceability Team
descriptionHtml:
The AWS Data Center Availability Serviceability team works with hundreds of AWS data centers globally to deliver the highest quality and lowest cost availability, capacity, and scaling results for our customers. We standardize operations globally by delivering tools, policy, processes, and procedures to our internal teams.

Serviceability is the ability to maintain, repair, and manage infrastructure assets efficiently throughout their lifecycle -- encompassing maintenance standards, spares management, training and certifications, operational readiness, and the systematic use of data and automation to prevent disruptions and drive continuous improvement.

We are seeking a Technical Program Manager to support serviceability for liquid cooling infrastructure in AWS data centers. Liquid cooling is a new and fast-growing technology that supports the next generation of high-density compute, including AI and machine learning workloads. This role will define how liquid-cooled equipment is maintained, serviced and kept ready to operate as we scale from early deployments to a global fleet.
What you will do:

You will support the serviceability program for liquid cooling across the AWS fleet. You will write and maintain preventive maintenance (PM) guidelines for liquid cooling components, such as coolant distribution, heat exchange and fluid management systems. You will build these guidelines with Operations, Data Center Engineering Operations (DCEO) and equipment vendors. You will partner with Finance on labor analyses that turn maintenance needs into staffing plans. You will work with Field Engineering to lead root cause analyses on maintenance and equipment findings, and you will make sure the lessons feed back into PM standards and procedures. You will work with Operations and site teams to build operational readiness plans for new liquid-cooled sites, then track readiness so every site is ready to operate safely and reliably from day one. You will also run field trials and stakeholder workshops to check procedures, collect feedback and drive continuous improvement.

Key job responsibilities
Own the execution and success metrics for liquid cooling serviceability across the global fleet
Write and maintain PM guidelines for liquid cooling components, working with Operations, DCEO and vendors
Conduct labor analyses with Finance to support annual and long-range staffing plans
Lead root cause analyses with Field Engineering on maintenance and equipment findings, and drive corrective actions into standards
Build operational readiness plans with Operations and site teams, and track readiness as new sites deploy
Run field trials and stakeholder workshops to validate procedures and collect operational feedback
Build mechanisms that keep serviceability standards current as the fleet grows and new equipment and vendors are introduced
Use data and metrics to measure program health, prioritize effort and report progress
Write narratives (one to six pages) and present to Director-level leadership
Travel up to 10–15%

Basic qualifications

- Bachelor's degree in mechanical engineering or equivalent
- 3+ years of technical product or program management experience

- Experience managing serviceability/maintenance programs

Preferred qualifications

title: Software Development Engineer II
descriptionHtml:
Most cloud engineers never see the physical world their software touches. On this team, you will. We build the networking that carries AWS out of the cloud and into customers' own data centers—so a hospital, a factory, or a bank can run AWS right next to the systems and data that can't leave the building. When you ship here, your code is soon routing real production traffic on real hardware in the field, all over the world.

In this role you'll design and build the services that keep that traffic flowing, and you'll own them all the way through—not just writing the code, but operating it, watching how it behaves in production, and making it more reliable over time. You'll dig into genuinely hard problems in distributed systems and networking, where the failure modes are interesting and the impact of a fix is immediate and visible.

You'll also help us work smarter, not just harder: a real part of the job is building AI agents and automation that take the repetitive engineering and operational work off the team's plate, so everyone can spend more time on the problems that actually need human judgment. If you like owning things end to end, want your work to matter in the physical world, and enjoy making a team faster as you go, you'll fit right in.

Key job responsibilities
- Design, build, test, and operate scalable, highly available control plane, distribution, and data plane services that route production traffic for AWS Outposts deployments worldwide.
- Own significant components end to end—from design documents and implementation through deployment, monitoring, and long-term operational health.
- Take ambiguous, loosely defined problems and drive them to well-reasoned technical designs, making sound tradeoffs with limited guidance.
- Write, update, and improve AI agents and automation that increase software-development and operational efficiency—reducing manual toil so the team can focus on high-judgment work.
- Raise the operational bar: improve observability, harden deployment pipelines, and drive down the time-to-detect and time-to-mitigate for the systems you own.
- Participate in an on-call rotation for the services you own, and lead the investigation and resolution of production issues, including root-cause analysis and long-term corrective actions.
- Write high-quality, well-tested, maintainable code and hold a high bar in design and code reviews.
- Brainstorm ideas with teammates and review key technical decisions and designs with senior engineers and leadership to pressure-test approaches and align on direction.
- Mentor junior engineers, share context generously, and contribute to the technical direction and engineering standards of the team.
- Collaborate across teams—partner service teams (e.g., S3, EBS, Route 53), networking, and hardware/edge teams—to deliver features that span organizational boundaries.

A day in the life
Most of your day is spent designing, building, and operating the services that route traffic for AWS Outposts and Local Gateway, keeping them running reliably for customers around the world. You'll write and review code, and you'll keep an eye on your dashboards to make sure the changes you ship are flowing safely into production and everything you own is healthy.

You'll also spend real time making the team faster: building and improving AI agents and automation that take routine engineering and operational work off everyone's plate, so we can focus on the harder, more interesting problems. Ideas come from everywhere here, so expect to brainstorm with teammates, sketch out approaches together, and talk through your bigger technical decisions with experienced engineers and leaders who'll help you sharpen your thinking. You'll also work closely with partner teams like S3, EBS, and Route 53 to ship things that span more than one service.

Beyond the day-to-day, you'll have the room to dig into ambiguous problems, decide how the services you own should evolve, and help the engineers around you grow. Because our software runs in customer data centers all over the world, you'll see the real impact of your work quickly—and you'll have a genuine say in how we make it more reliable and easier to operate over time.


About the team
Our team is focused on building reliable, scalable software that customers depend on every day. We value collaboration, clear communication, and a commitment to getting the details right. We believe that great software comes from inclusive teams where every voice is heard and good ideas can come from anyone. As we look ahead, we are investing in new capabilities and technologies that will expand our impact, and you will play a key role in shaping that direction. If you are excited about solving hard problems alongside thoughtful engineers, we would love to hear from you.

Basic qualifications

- 3+ years of non-internship professional software development experience
- 2+ years of non-internship design or architecture (design patterns, reliability and scaling) of new and existing systems experience
- 1+ years of software development engineer or related occupational experience
- 1+ years of designing and developing large-scale, multi-tiered, multi-threaded, embedded or distributed software applications, tools, systems, and services using: C#, C++, Java, or Perl experience
- 1+ years of Object Oriented Design experience
- Bachelor's degree or foreign equivalent in Computer Science, Engineering, Mathematics, or a related field
- Experience programming with at least one software programming language

Preferred qualifications

- 3+ years of full software development life cycle, including coding standards, code reviews, source control management, build processes, testing, and operations experience
- Bachelor's degree in computer science or equivalent

descriptionHtml:
As a member of the Global Controls Team, you will collaborate with highly motivated operators, engineers and technicians in the data center industry to maintain and optimize critical infrastructure systems. You will be responsible for troubleshooting and maintaining the Building Management System (BMS) and Electrical Power Monitoring System (EPMS) while developing new processes and standards that drive innovation in the controls space.

AWS data centers utilize sophisticated industrial control systems to automatically operate mechanical equipment, maintaining optimal temperature and pressure conditions throughout the facilities. These systems integrate and monitor multiple critical components, including generators, uninterruptible power sources, diesel generators, electrical switchgear, power distribution units, variable frequency drives, automatic and static transfer switches, air-cooled and water-cooled chillers, pumps, cooling towers, heat exchangers, Computer Room Air Handlers (CRAHs), and air economizers. Within this industrial control system infrastructure, the BMS serves as the primary control platform for all mechanical systems within the data center, while the EPMS functions as the primary monitoring platform for all electrical systems. This position offers the opportunity to work with cutting-edge technology in mission-critical environments while contributing to the reliability and efficiency of AWS's global infrastructure.

title: Software Development Engineer, WW Returns and Recommerce
descriptionHtml:
Not many teams aspire to zero. Welcome to the Worldwide Returns and ReCommerce team (WWR&R) at Amazon.com.

WW R&R is an agile, innovative organization dedicated to ‘making zero happen’ to benefit our customers, our company, and the environment. The mission of WWR&R is to eliminate defects that cause returns (Zero defects), deliver Zero cost of returns for Amazon and send Zero product waste to landfill “the 3 Zeros”. We do this by developing products and driving unparalleled operational excellence to help customers keep what they buy, recover returned & damaged product value, and create the best customer returns experience in the world.
Amazon WW R&R is comprised of business, product, operational, program, software engineering and data teams that manage the life of a returned or damaged product from a customer to the warehouse and on to its next best use. Our work is broad and deep: we train machine learning models to automate routing and find signals to optimize re-use; we invent new channels to give products a second life; we develop world-class product support to help customers love what they buy; we pilot smarter product evaluations; we work from the customer backward to find ways to make the return experience remarkably delightful and easy; and we do it all while scrutinizing our business with laser focus.

As a member of this team, your mission will be to design, develop, document and support massively scalable, distributed real time systems. Using C++, Java, object oriented design patterns, distributed databases and other innovative storage techniques, you will build and deliver software systems that support complex and rapidly evolving business requirements.

We are looking for software engineers with 4+ years of solid Software engineering experience involving solving complex problems. They will get to work on some of the key initiatives planned to support our rapid evolution and growth and in the process solve some of the most challenging problems. These engineers will provide the technical leadership to the team, drive best practices, mentor other engineers and drive continuous improvements in engineering excellence.
We are a group that has fun at work while driving incredible customer, business, and environmental impact. We are backed by a strong leadership group dedicated to operational excellence that empowers a reasonable work-life balance. As an established, experienced team, we offer the scope and support needed for substantial career growth.

Amazon is earth’s most customer-centric company and through WW R&R, the earth is our customer too. Come join us and innovate with the Amazon Worldwide Returns & ReCommerce team!

2+ years of non-internship design or architecture (design patterns, reliability and scaling) of new and existing systems experience
Experience programming with at least one software programming language

title: Software Development Engineer, Elastic Block Store
descriptionHtml:
Do you want to build the data platform that shows how a cloud storage service used by millions of AWS customers is behaving? As a Software Development Engineer on Amazon Elastic Block Store (EBS), you will design, build and operate a self-service telemetry platform that processes petabytes of data every day across every AWS Region. Engineers across EBS and AWS rely on it for both operational and analytical needs, from automated production decisions and real-time monitoring to compliance reporting, customer insights and capacity forecasting. You will own large-scale distributed systems end to end, make them more efficient at scale, and help shape how engineers and AI-powered tools access data. If you are curious about distributed systems, data platforms and cloud storage, we would like to hear from you.

Key job responsibilities
- Design, build and operate distributed systems that transform, store, query and export petabyte-scale telemetry data
- Improve cost efficiency by evolving the platform architecture, adopting new languages and technologies, and building mechanisms that keep cost under control as usage grows
- Build programmatic and AI-ready interfaces that give engineers and automated tools secure, access-controlled access to data
- Raise operational quality through monitoring, alarming, data-quality validation and automated recovery
- Partner with software engineers, data engineers and product managers across EBS to turn specific use cases into reusable platform features

A day in the life
Your day might start with a short team sync, followed by focused time on the project you lead, such as designing a new storage layout or optimizing the efficiency of the transform or query engines. Along the way, you join design brainstorms and reviews, review teammates' code and get feedback on your own, and may meet with an EBS team that wants to bring new data onto the platform to help them shape the solution. You also join an on-call rotation, typically one week about every eight weeks. When you get paged, you have runbooks and your teammates to support you, and after each page we review the steps together to prevent it from happening again or automate the response.

About the team
Our team owns the telemetry and analytics platform that EBS relies on for operational and business insight, and our vision is to be the single observability platform for EBS. Our customers are EBS engineering, data engineering and product teams, along with other AWS teams that build on EBS data. Over the next few years, we are focused on making the platform more efficient, unifying how data is transformed and queried, and making data accessible to AI-powered tools. We stay on top of new technologies and actively use AI-driven development in our daily work. We invest in fault tolerance and automation so operational load stays low, which keeps our team sustainable, frees most of our time for delivering new features, and supports a healthy work-life balance. We have a mix of experience levels and tenures, and we invest in your growth through projects that expand your scope, designs with impact across EBS, and mentorship from senior engineers.

Basic qualifications

- 3+ years of non-internship professional software development experience
- 2+ years of non-internship design or architecture (design patterns, reliability and scaling) of new and existing systems experience
- Experience programming with at least one software programming language

Preferred qualifications

- 3+ years of full software development life cycle, including coding standards, code reviews, source control management, build processes, testing, and operations experience
- Bachelor's degree in computer science or equivalent

Project durations vary from a few days to several months, with travel across North America. This is a travel-based role and you will be expected to travel to meet the requirements of your projects across North America, upwards of 75% or more.

As a Systems Engineer in RDPI, you will be overseeing large scale project planning, installation, and launch of industrial automation technologies across Amazons growing Stores network. This field engineering position demands strong technical skills for deploying robotic equipment, including mechanical and electrical systems, network configurations, and software coordination. The ideal candidate has experience with complex electro-mechanical and network systems, demonstrating leadership in installation, maintenance, upgrades, and troubleshooting of technologies being deployed across North America.

You will work with cross-functional partners across our engineering, product strategy, software, supply chain, third-party installers, contracted deployment engineers, construction teams, and internal operations customer teams, functioning as the lead on-site project manager to provide technical oversight on installation Amazon-designed automation equipment. This Systems Engineer position is an individual contributor role, influencing and leading stakeholders from planning through go-live of each project. Candidates should have a proven track record of successfully leading multiple concurrent projects across one or more automation solutions.

Key job responsibilities
As a Systems Engineer I, you will work with a team of 1-5 engineers and collaborate with an on-site project manager to provide technical oversight on the installation of both third party and Amazon designed robotics equipment that may be in various phases of the product life cycle. These deployments require extensive collaboration with various stakeholders, including third-party installers, contracted engineers, construction, hardware, software, IT, and other partner teams. Strong communication skills are essential for interacting with both internal and external partners and customers. As an Amazonian, you must demonstrate independent initiative to identify and solve problems in real time during deployments. A strong technical understanding, love for field work, and a keen interest in diving deep into the understanding of Amazon’s robotics systems are key attributes for this role.

- You will support and guide installation of robotics, packaging and sortation technologies at Amazon fulfillment centers
- You will develop detailed knowledge of the operation of robotic systems and guide installation, commissioning, and troubleshooting of these systems both on site and remotely
- You will manage technical ambiguity around integration of work cells in fulfillment centers
- You will collaborate with hardware engineering, technical program managers, product managers, and internal customers including site maintenance and operations teams
- You will travel to project sites and collaborate both virtually and in person to ensure all business stakeholders are aligned on program status
- You will manage day to day project scheduling and budget management
- You will work on continuous improvement activities to improve the projects in your space
- You will generate and implement continuous improvement ideas around work-scopes
- You will lead teams of other engineers on projects
- You will travel to both live warehouses and new construction sites, the scopes may vary significantly in length and include heavy travel
- You will travel to project sites across North America, upwards of 75% or more


A day in the life
In this role you will be focused on execution of end-to-end deployment and manage technical ambiguity around integration of workcells in fulfillment centers. On a daily basis you will collaborate with hardware engineering, technical program managers, product managers, and internal customers including site maintenance and operations teams, to ensure the product you are deploying, is both ready for deployment and capable of achieving the business requirements. You will travel to your project sites, collaborate both virtually and in person, to ensure all business stakeholders are aligned on program status. You will manage the day-to-day project execution, and work on continuous improvement activities to improve the projects in your space. You will spend time with mentors and your manager to develop your professional skills and collaborate amongst your team to move the needle on the services you are accountable for.

We are a smart, collaborative team of enthusiastic doers that work passionately to apply innovative advances in robotics and software to solve real-world challenges that will transform our customers’ experiences in ways we can’t even image yet. title: Principal Technical Program Manager, Fauna
descriptionHtml:
Fauna Robotics is building capable, safe, and delightful robots for everyday life. We are hiring a Principal Technical Program Manager to lead how robot software ships at Fauna. Our products improve with each software release: new features and skills make robots already in the hands of developers and partners more useful.

In this role, you will own the software release program end-to-end, from planning to deployment. This includes how we move research into the product, how hardware changes are reflected in software, and how we deliver a great software experience to customers. You will build the planning mechanisms for the software organization, drive excellence in execution, and lead our largest launches

Key job responsibilities
- Own the robot software release program: cadence, go/no-go criteria, staged rollouts, and rollback decisions

- Collaborate with hardware, firmware, science, and manufacturing programs so that robot software is ready to ship on time and with high quality

- Build roadmaps, dependency tracking, and status reporting for the software org and own the integration plan for major launches and demos

- Define release quality bars with QA and engineering, and use test results, telemetry, and field reports to decide when to ship

- Set the multi-year plan for how Fauna ships robot software as the fleet and the org grow, and build mechanisms for the long term

- Find problems that recur across teams and fix the process that causes them, and handle escalations as they happen across the program

- Present program status, risks, and tradeoffs to senior leadership

About the team
Fauna Robotics, an Amazon company, is building capable, safe, and genuinely delightful robots for everyday life. Our goal is simple: make robots people actually want to live and interact with in everyday human spaces.

We believe that future won't arrive until building for robotics becomes far more accessible. Today, too much effort is spent reinventing the fundamentals. We're changing that by developing tightly integrated hardware and software systems that make it faster, safer, and more intuitive to create real-world robotic products.

Our work spans the full stack: mechanical design, control systems, dynamic modeling, and intelligent software. The focus is not just functionality, but experience. We're building robots that feel responsive, expressive, and genuinely useful.

At Fauna, you'll work at the frontier of this space, helping define how robots move, manipulate, and interact with people in natural environments. It's an opportunity to solve hard problems across hardware and software with a team focused on making robotics accessible and joyful to build.

If you care about making robotics real for everyone and building systems that are as delightful as they are capable, we're interested in hearing from you.

- 10+ years of working directly with engineering teams experience
- 5+ years of software development experience

- Experience leading software release programs for products that run on physical devices, such as robots, vehicles, consumer electronics, or connected home devices

Preferred qualifications

- Experience aligning software releases with hardware development stages (EVT, DVT, PVT)

- Experience running releases for developer-facing products such as SDKs or APIs
